instead of ${\mathfrak a}_2$ due to the presence of the gradient
$\nabla \rho$.

Without the indicators, we may apply Lemma \ref{s32} with
$1/\gamma = \Vert J\Vert_\infty$ to conclude that
\begin{align*}
& \int \Big|\, \sum_{{\mathtt k}\in \Sigma^+_{L_2}}  
W_J ({\mathtt k})  \,
\big \{ \, G({\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}}) \, - \,
E_{\nu^n_{\rho(\cdot)}} [\, G({\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}}) \,] \, \big\}
\, \Big |\, f\, d\nu^n_{\rho(\cdot)}
\,\le\, \Vert J\Vert_\infty \, \Big\{\, 
\Big[  \, H_n (f\,|\, \nu^n_{\rho(\cdot)})
\,+\, \ln(2) \, \Big] \,+\, n^{d-2}  \,\Big\} \,.
\end{align*}
To complete the proof of the lemma, it remains to recollect all
previous estimates, and to observe that $n^{d-2} \le (\ell_1/n)^2\,
n^d$.
<!-- end proof-16 -->
<!-- remark-15: body_md -->
This remainder should be smaller than that obtained in Lemma \ref{s69}
due to the extra factor $\ell^{-d}_1$ coming from
$\Gamma_{{\mathtt k}}^{-1}$.  Indeed, in \eqref{169} we have
$(\ell_1/n)^2 \ell^{-d}_1$ instead of the $(\ell_1/n)^2$ that appears
in Lemma \ref{s69}. However, there is also the term
$n^{-1} \ell^{-d}_1$, which is not comparable to $(\ell_1/n)^2$. This
happens because in Corollary \ref{s31} we roughly estimated the
first-order term of Lemma \ref{s15}, which is sufficient for our
purposes. We could have taken this term into account and proceeded as
in Lemma \ref{s69} to obtain a better estimate.
<!-- end remark-15 -->
<!-- proof-17: body_md -->
By \eqref{170}, Lemma \ref{s33} and the paragraph right after the
statement of this lemma, it is enough to estimate \eqref{171}.

In \eqref{175} we decomposed $W^{\rm exp}_{x,A}$ as the sum of
$W^{{\rm e}, 1}_{x,A}$ and $W^{{\rm e}, 2}_{x,A}$. Equation
\eqref{174} provides an estimate for
$W^{{\rm e}, 2}_{x,A} \, -\, E_{\nu^n_{\rho(\cdot)}} \big[ {\mathtt 1}_{\delta_1} ({\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}}) \, W^{{\rm e},2}_{x,A} \big] $.  Lemma
\ref{s69} and equation \eqref{169}, noting the form of $W_{{\mathtt k}, A}$
in \eqref{168} and $F({\textsf m}) = {\mathtt q}_A({\textsf m})$ in the paragraph
after the proof of Lemma \ref{s69}, present an estimate for
$[\, W^{{\rm e}, 1}_{x,A} - W_{{\mathtt k}, A}\,] \, -\,
E_{\nu^n_{\rho(\cdot)}} \big[ {\mathtt 1}_{\delta_1} ({\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}}) \,
[\, W^{{\rm e},1}_{x,A} - W_{{\mathtt k}, A}\,] \,\big] $.


To complete the proof of the proposition, it remains to recollect the
remainders obtained in these steps, and to observe that
$(\ell_1/n) \, \ell^{-2d}_1 \le (1/n) \ell^{-d}_1$.
<!-- end proof-17 -->
<!-- remark-16: body_md -->
\label{r09}
Suppose that ${\mathfrak p}$ is the polynomial ${\mathfrak p}_A$ introduced in the
statement of Theorem \ref{s01}:
${\color{blue} {\mathfrak p}_A (\rho)} := {\mathtt p}_A (\rho) + \ell_1^{-d} {\mathtt q}_A
(\rho)$.  Substituting ${\mathfrak p}$ by ${\mathfrak p}_A$ in equation \eqref{111}
with ${\mathtt t}_1 = \ell_1$, a cancellation of the $\ell_1^{-d}$- order
terms occurs and yields that
\begin{equation*}
W_{{\mathfrak p}_A}  ({\textsf m}) \,=\, {\mathtt p}_A({\textsf m}) \,+\, \frac{1}{2\,\ell_1^{2d}}\,
{\mathtt q}_{A}''({\textsf m})\, \chi({\textsf m})\,.
\end{equation*}

This cancellation simplifies considerably the proof in dimension $d=3$
as it eliminates the problematic terms of order $\ell_1^{-d}$ which
would require careful attention. On the one hand, it is a fortuitous
cancellation as the correction terms in Theorems \ref{s01} and
\ref{s26} have different origins.  The corrector term
$\ell_1^{-d} {\mathtt q}_A (\rho)$ in Theorem \ref{s01} is produced by the
first order term in the equivalence of ensembles, while the corrector
term \eqref{111} in Theorem \ref{s26} is produced by the expansion of
$E_{\nu_\rho} [ {\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}}^{|A|}]$ as a function of $\rho$. The
$0$-order term is $\rho^{|A|}$ and the first order one is
$(1/2) |A| (|A|-1) \rho^{|A|-2} \chi(\rho)\, |B_{{\mathtt k}}|^{-1}$.

On the other hand, in our multi-scale scheme, we replace ${\mathtt p}_A$ by
its canonical expectation on a block of width $\ell_1$.  If now,
instead of approximating by the equivalence of ensembles and then a
further reduction of the associated grand canonical quantity, we would
state the approximation by the conditional expectation on a block of
width $\ell_1\ell_2$ directly, the cancellation would not be seen at
all.
<!-- end remark-16 -->
<!-- theorem-5: body_md -->
\label{s26}
Let $\rho\colon {\mathbb T}^d \to [0,1]$ be a density profile of class $C^3$
satisfying \eqref{83}.  Fix a polynomial
${\mathfrak p}\colon [0,1] \to {\mathbb R}$, a function $J\colon {\mathbb T}^d \to {\mathbb R}$
of class $C^1$, and constants $\delta>0$, $\epsilon>0$, $K_1\ge 1 $,
$K_2\ge 1$.  Then, there exist finite constants
${\mathfrak a}_{3,3} = {\mathfrak a}_{3,3} ({\mathfrak p})$,
${\mathfrak b}_1 = {\mathfrak b}_1({\mathfrak r}, \Vert \rho\Vert_{C^3}, {\mathfrak p})$, $C_1$, and
$C_2 = C_2({\mathfrak p})$ such that
\begin{equation*}
\begin{aligned}
& \int
\sum_{{\mathtt j} \in \Sigma^+_{{\mathtt t}_3}}
\sum_{{\mathtt k} \in \Lambda_{{\mathtt j}}}  {\mathtt t}_1^d\, J_{{\mathtt k}}\,
\Big\{\,   {\mathfrak p}({\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}})
- E_{\nu^n_{\rho(\cdot)}} [ \, {\mathfrak p}({\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}})\, ] 
\,-\, 
\big(\, W_{{\mathfrak p}} ({\textsf m}_{2, {\mathtt j}})
- E_{\nu^n_{\rho(\cdot)}} [ W_{{\mathfrak p}} ({\textsf m}_{2, {\mathtt j}})] \,\big)
\, \Big\}\,
f\, d\nu^n_{\rho(\cdot)}
\\
&\quad  \le\, \delta\, n^2 \,  I_n  ( f \,;\, \nu^n_{\rho (\cdot)} )
\,+\, 
{\mathfrak a}_{3,3} \, \Vert J\Vert_{C^1} 
\,\Big\{   \, H_n (f\,|\, \nu^n_{\rho(\cdot)})\, + \, \ln(2)\,\Big\}
\,+\, C_1 \,  n^d\, 
\Big(\frac{{\mathtt t}_1{\mathtt t}_2}{n}\Big)^4
\\
&\quad 
\,+\, {\mathfrak a}_{3,3}\, \Vert J\Vert^2_{C^1} \,  n^d\, \Big\{ \,
\frac{1}{\delta}\, 
\frac{{\mathtt t}_2^{d+2}}{{\mathtt t}_1^{d-2}}   \, \frac{1}{n^2} 
\,+\,  e^{C_2 K_2^d}\, \frac{1 }{({\mathtt t}_1{\mathtt t}_2)^{d}} 
\, \frac{1 }{{\mathtt t}_1^{d}}   \, \Big\}
\\
&\quad 
\,+\, {\mathfrak a}_{3,3}\, \Vert J\Vert_{C^1} \,  n^d\,
\Big\{ 
\Big(\frac{{\mathtt t}_1{\mathtt t}_2} {n}\Big)^2 \, \frac{1}{({\mathtt t}_1{\mathtt t}_2)^{d/2}}
\,+\, 
\frac{{\mathtt t}_1{\mathtt t}_2 }{n} \, \frac{1} {({\mathtt t}_1{\mathtt t}_2)^d } \,
\,+\, \Big(\frac{{\mathtt t}_1 }{n} \Big)^2 \, \frac{1 }{{\mathtt t}_1^{d}}  \Big\}
\end{aligned}
\end{equation*}
for all integers ${\mathtt t}_1\ge 2$, ${\mathtt t}_2\ge 2$ such that
$({\mathtt t}_1{\mathtt t}_2)^{d+3} \le K_1\, n^3$,
$({\mathtt t}_1{\mathtt t}_2)^{1+(d/4)} \le n$, ${\mathtt t}_2 \le K_2\, {\mathtt t}_1$,
${\mathtt t}_2^{2+d} \le (\delta / {\mathfrak c}_{\rm LS}) (n/{\mathtt t}_1)^2 \, ({\mathfrak b}_1
\wedge {\mathtt t}_1^{-\epsilon})$, and densities $f$ with respect to
$\nu^n_{\rho(\cdot)}$. In this formula,
$C_1 = \exp\{{\mathfrak c}_{\rm LS} K_1 [1+{\mathfrak a}_{3,3}]\,[1+\Vert
J\Vert_{C^1}]/\delta\} \, \exp\{{\mathfrak a}_{3,3} K_2^d\}$.
<!-- end theorem-5 -->
<!-- remark-17: body_md -->
In this article, Theorem \ref{s26} will only be used with $K_2=1$. We
stated it in this generality as it might be useful in other models. On
the other hand, in $d=3$, in the second step $K_1$ is chosen equal to
$1$, and in the third $K_1=\kappa^6$, where $\kappa$ is a constant
which converges to $+\infty$ after $n\to +\infty$.
<!-- end remark-17 -->
<!-- remark-18: body_md -->
\label{r07}
We observed in Remark \ref{rm3} that Theorem \ref{s01} and Corollary
\ref{s46} reach sufficiently large cubes in dimension $1$, since they
allow intervals of length of order $\epsilon_n n^{2/3}$, while the
proof of the non-equilibrium fluctuations only requires cubes of
length $K \, n^{1/2}$, for some $1\ll K\ll n$. Thus, Theorem
\ref{s26}, though valid in dimension $1$, will only be used in
dimensions $2$ and $3$. Corollary \ref{s48} states that in dimension
$2$, the correction term in $W_{{\mathfrak p}} ({\textsf m}_{2, {\mathtt j}})$ appearing
in the statement of Theorem \ref{s26} is not needed.
<!-- end remark-18 -->
<!-- remark-19: body_md -->
As observed above, the correction term in
$W_{{\mathfrak p}} ({\textsf m}_{2, {\mathtt j}}) $ is the same as the one obtained in
Theorem \ref{s01} in the first step of the multiscale analysis, but
with a negative sign. It comes from the replacement of
$E_{\nu^n_{\rho(\cdot)}} [{\mathfrak p}({\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}})]$ by
${\mathfrak p}(E_{\nu^n_{\rho(\cdot)}} [{\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}}])$. We need
${\mathfrak p}(\cdot)$ to be a polynomial because we are only able to estimate
powers of ${\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}}$, that is, ${\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}}^p$, $p\ge 1$.
<!-- end remark-19 -->
<!-- remark-20: body_md -->
One of the main challenges in the proof of the hydrodynamic limit or
the convergence of the density field to the solution of some SPDE
consists in replacing the average of local functions by a function of
the density over a large box. Theorem \ref{s26} provides a method to
increase the width of the box. Its proof does not rely on specific
properties of the model. It might therefore be of independent
interest.
<!-- end remark-20 -->
<!-- remark-21: body_md -->
In dimension $d=3$, the condition
$({\mathtt t}_1{\mathtt t}_2)^{d+3} \le K_1\, n^3$, that is,
${\mathtt t}_1{\mathtt t}_2 \le K'_1\, n^{1/2}$ prevents us from reaching cubes
of length larger than $K'_1 \, n^{1/2}$.
<!-- end remark-21 -->
<!-- corollary-5: body_md -->
\label{s48}
Fix a polynomial ${\mathfrak p}\colon [0,1] \to {\mathbb R}$, a function
$J\colon {\mathbb T}^d \to {\mathbb R}$ of class $C^1$, and constants $\delta>0$,
$\epsilon>0$, $K_1\ge 1$.  Then, there exist finite
constants ${\mathfrak a}_{3,3} = {\mathfrak a}_{3,3} ({\mathfrak p})$,
${\mathfrak b}_1 = {\mathfrak b}_1({\mathfrak r}, \Vert \rho\Vert_{C^3}, {\mathfrak p})$ such that
\begin{equation*}
\begin{aligned}
& \int
\sum_{{\mathtt j} \in \Sigma^+_{{\mathtt t}_3}}
\sum_{{\mathtt k} \in \Lambda_{{\mathtt j}}}  {\mathtt t}_1^d\, J_{{\mathtt k}}\, \Big\{\, 
{\mathfrak p}({\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}}) 
- E_{\nu^n_{\rho(\cdot)}} [\, {\mathfrak p}({\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}})\, ] 
\,-\, 
\big(\, {\mathfrak p}({\textsf m}_{2, {\mathtt j}})
- E_{\nu^n_{\rho(\cdot)}} [\, {\mathfrak p}({\textsf m}_{2, {\mathtt j}}) \, ] \,\big)
\, \Big\}\,
f\, d\nu^n_{\rho(\cdot)}
\\
&\quad
\le\, \delta\, n^2 \,  I_n  ( f \,;\, \nu^n_{\rho (\cdot)} )
\,+\, 
{\mathfrak a}_{3,3} \, \Vert J\Vert_{C^1} 
\,\Big\{   \, H_n (f\,|\, \nu^n_{\rho(\cdot)})\, + \, \ln(2)\,\Big\}
\,+\, {\mathtt C} (J)\,  n^d\, 
\Big(\frac{{\mathtt t}_1{\mathtt t}_2}{n}\Big)^4
\\
&\quad 
\,+\, {\mathfrak a}_{3,3}\, (1+\Vert J\Vert_{C^1})^2 \,  n^d\, \Big\{ \,
\frac{1}{\delta}\, 
\frac{{\mathtt t}_2^{d+2}}{{\mathtt t}_1^{d-2}}   \, \frac{1}{n^2} 
\,+\,  \frac{1 }{({\mathtt t}_1{\mathtt t}_2)^{d/2}} 
\, \frac{1 }{{\mathtt t}_1^{d}}   \, \Big\}
\\
&\quad 
\,+\, {\mathfrak a}_{3,3}\, \Vert J\Vert_{C^1} \,  n^d\,
\Big\{ 
\Big(\frac{{\mathtt t}_1{\mathtt t}_2} {n}\Big)^2 \, \frac{1}{({\mathtt t}_1{\mathtt t}_2)^{d/2}}
\,+\, 
\frac{{\mathtt t}_1{\mathtt t}_2 }{n} \, \frac{1} {({\mathtt t}_1{\mathtt t}_2)^d } \,
\,+\, \Big(\frac{{\mathtt t}_1 }{n} \Big)^2 \, \frac{1 }{{\mathtt t}_1^{d}}  \Big\}
\end{aligned}
\end{equation*}
for all integers ${\mathtt t}_1\ge 2$, ${\mathtt t}_2\ge 2$ such that
$({\mathtt t}_1{\mathtt t}_2)^{d+3} \le K_1\, n^3$,
$({\mathtt t}_1{\mathtt t}_2)^{1+(d/4)} \le n$, ${\mathtt t}_2 \le {\mathtt t}_1$,
${\mathtt t}_2^{2+d} \le (\delta / {\mathfrak c}_{\rm LS}) (n/{\mathtt t}_1)^2 \, ({\mathfrak b}_1
\wedge {\mathtt t}_1^{-\epsilon})$, and densities $f$ with respect to
$\nu^n_{\rho(\cdot)}$. In this formula,
${\mathtt C}(J)  = \exp\{{\mathfrak c}_{\rm LS} K_1 [1+{\mathfrak a}_{3,3}]\,[1+\Vert
J\Vert_{C^1}]/\delta\}$.
<!-- end corollary-5 -->
<!-- proof-18: body_md -->
In view of Theorem \ref{s26}, we need to estimate the correction term
in $W_{{\mathfrak p}} ({\textsf m}_{2, {\mathtt j}})$. Recall that 
${\mathfrak q} (x) :=  -\, (1/2)\, {\mathfrak p}'' (x)\, \chi (x)$,
$J_{2, {\mathtt j}} := \sum_{{\mathtt k} \in \Lambda_{{\mathtt j}}} J_{{\mathtt k}}$. Clearly,
$\Vert J_{2, {\mathtt j}}\Vert_\infty \le {\mathtt t}_2^{d} \, \Vert
J\Vert_\infty$. As ${\mathtt t}_2\le {\mathtt t}_1$,
$\Vert J_{2, {\mathtt j}}\Vert_\infty \le \Vert J\Vert_\infty \, ({\mathtt t}_1{\mathtt t}_2)^{d/2}$.  Therefore, by Lemma \ref{s45} with
$r_1={\mathtt t}_1{\mathtt t}_2$ and ${\mathfrak a}({\mathtt j}) = J_{2, {\mathtt j}}$,
using  ${\mathtt t}_2\le {\mathtt t}_1$ again,
\begin{align*}
& \int \sum_{{\mathtt j} \in \Sigma^+_{{\mathtt t}_3}}
J_{2, {\mathtt j}}
\, \Big\{\, {\mathfrak q}( {\textsf m}_{2,{\mathtt j}})
- E_{\nu^n_{\rho(\cdot)}} [\, {\mathfrak q}( {\textsf m}_{2,{\mathtt j}})\, ]
\, \Big\}\, f \, d\nu^n_{\rho(\cdot)}
\\
&\quad \,\le \,
C({\mathfrak p})\,  \Vert J\Vert_\infty \, \Big\{\, 
\, H_n(f \,|\, \nu^n_{\rho (\cdot)}  )
\,+\, 
\Big(\frac{1}{{\mathtt t}_1{\mathtt t}_2} \Big)^{d/2}\, 
\Big(\frac{n}{{\mathtt t}_1} \Big)^d \,\Big\} \,.
\end{align*}
This additional error is to be added to the right-hand side of Theorem
\ref{s26} statement.  This error is larger than the existing error
$(n/{\mathtt t}_1)^d\, ({\mathtt t}_1{\mathtt t}_2)^{-d}$, and replaces it in the
statement of Corollary \ref{s48}. This completes the proof.
<!-- end proof-18 -->
<!-- proposition-3: body_md -->
\label{s37}
Fix $\delta>0$, $\epsilon>0$, a polynomial ${\mathfrak p}(\cdot)$, a function
$J\colon {\mathbb T}^d \to {\mathbb R}$ of class $C^1$, and $K_1\ge 1$.  Then,
there exist finite constants ${\mathfrak a}_{3,1}$, ${\mathfrak a}_{3,3}$ and
${\mathfrak b}_1 = {\mathfrak b}_1({\mathfrak r}, \Vert \rho\Vert_{C^3}, {\mathfrak p})$ such that
\begin{equation*}
\begin{aligned}
\sum_{{\mathtt j} \in \Sigma^+_{{\mathtt t}_3}}
\int  {\mathtt 1}\{ {\textsf m}_{2, {\mathtt j}} \in ({\mathfrak r}_- ,  {\mathfrak r}_+) \}
\sum_{{\mathtt k} \in \Lambda_{{\mathtt j}}} {\mathtt t}^d_1\,   J_{{\mathtt k}}\,
\big\{\, {\mathfrak p}({\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}}) \,-\,
E_{\nu^{\rm c} _{2,{\mathtt j}, {\textsf M}} } [\, {\mathfrak p}({\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}}) 
\,]  \,\big\} \, f\;
d\nu^n_{\rho(\cdot)}
\\
\,\le\,
\delta\, n^2 \,  I_n  ( f \,;\, \nu^n_{\rho (\cdot)} ) \,+\,
\frac{{\mathfrak a}_{3,3}}{\delta}\,
\Big\{\, {\mathfrak c}_{\rm LS} \, {\mathfrak C}_2
\Big(\frac{{\mathtt t}_1{\mathtt t}_2}{n}\Big)^4\, n^d
\,+\,  \Vert J\Vert^2_\infty\,
{\mathtt t}_2^{d+2}  \, \Big( \frac{n}{{\mathtt t}_1}\Big)^{d-2} \,\Big\}
\end{aligned}
\end{equation*}
for all densities $f$ with respect to $\nu^n_{\rho(\cdot)}$, and all
${\mathtt t}_1\ge 2$, ${\mathtt t}_2\ge 2$ such that
$({\mathtt t}_1{\mathtt t}_2)^{d+3} \le K_1\, n^3$,
${\mathtt t}_2^{2+d} \le (\delta / {\mathfrak c}_{\rm LS}) \Vert J\Vert_\infty^{-1}\,
(n/{\mathtt t}_1)^2 \, ({\mathfrak b}_1 \wedge {\mathtt t}_1^{-\epsilon})$.  In this
equation,
${\mathfrak C}_2 = \exp\{ {\mathfrak c}_{\rm LS} C_0({\mathfrak p})\, K_1 \, (\, {\mathfrak a}_{3,1} +
\Vert J\Vert_{C^1})/\delta\}$.
<!-- end proposition-3 -->
<!-- lemma-14: body_md -->
\label{s16}
Fix $\epsilon>0$, $0<\delta < 1/2$, and a polynomial
${\mathfrak p}\colon [0,1]\to {\mathbb R}$.  Then, there exist finite constants
${\mathfrak a}_{3,3} = {\mathfrak a}_{3,3}({\mathfrak p}(\cdot), \delta)$,
${\mathfrak a}^*_{3,3} = {\mathfrak a}^*_{3,3}({\mathfrak p}(\cdot), \delta)$,
$C_0 = C_0(\epsilon)$ such that
\begin{equation*}
\max_{{\mathtt j} \in \Sigma^+_{{\mathtt t}_3}} \max_{{\mathtt k} \in \Lambda_{{\mathtt j}}}
\sup_{ \delta \le  {\textsf m} \le 1-\delta}
\ln  E_{\nu^{\rm c} _{2,{\mathtt j}, {\textsf M}} } 
\big[ \, e^{ \beta \, {\mathtt t}_1^d \, \widehat{{\mathfrak p}} ({\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}})
}\,  \big]
\; \le  \;  {\mathfrak a}_{3,3}\, C_0(\epsilon) \, \beta^2
\end{equation*}
for all ${\mathtt t}_1\ge 2$, and
$ \beta < \min\{ 1, 1/{\mathfrak a}^*_{3,3} , {\mathtt t}_1^{-\epsilon}\}$.
<!-- end lemma-14 -->
<!-- proof-19: body_md -->
Fix $0<\delta<1/2$. In this proof, all constants ${\mathfrak a}_i$,
$1\le i\le 3$, are allowed to depend on $\delta$ and the polynomial
${\mathfrak p}$, but not on $\epsilon$. The proof relies on two bounds of
$\widehat{{\mathfrak p}} (\cdot)$. 

We first affirm that there exists a finite constant ${\mathfrak a}_{3,3}$ such
that
\begin{equation}
\label{72}
\max_{{\mathtt j} \in \Sigma^+_{{\mathtt t}_3}} \max_{{\mathtt k} \in \Lambda_{{\mathtt j}}}
\sup_{ \delta \le  {\textsf m} \le 1-\delta}
E_{\nu^{\rm c} _{2,{\mathtt j}, {\textsf M}} }
\big[ \, \big\{\, {\mathtt t}_1^d \; \widehat{{\mathfrak p}}  ({\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}})
\big\}^2 \big] \; \le\; {\mathfrak a}_{3,3} \; .
\end{equation}
The proof of claim \eqref{72} relies on results presented in Appendix
\ref{sec12}. By Lemma \ref{s17}, in the definitions of
${\mathfrak p}_{{\mathtt j}, {\mathtt k}} (\cdot)$ and ${\textsf m}_{{\mathtt j}, {\mathtt k}}$, we may
replace the canonical measure by the grand canonical one at a cost
bounded by ${\mathfrak a}_1\, ({\mathtt t}_1{\mathtt t}_2)^{-d}$. It remains to estimate
the expectation in \eqref{72} with $\widehat{{\mathfrak p}} ({\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}})$
replaced by
\begin{align*}
{\mathfrak p}({\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}})
\,-\,  E_{\nu^{\rm gc} _{2,{\mathtt j}, {\textsf M}} } [{\mathfrak p}({\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}}) ]
- {\mathfrak p}'( \widetilde{{\textsf m}}_{{\mathtt j}, {\mathtt k}} )
\,\big[\, {\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}} - \widetilde{{\textsf m}}_{{\mathtt j}, {\mathtt k}} 
\,\big]\,.
\end{align*}
By Lemma \ref{s22} with $s_1={\mathtt t}_1$, $s_2={\mathtt t}_2$, the absolute
value of the difference between
$E_{\nu^{\rm gc} _{2,{\mathtt j}, {\textsf M}} } [{\mathfrak p}({\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}}) ]$ and
${\mathfrak p}(\widetilde{{\textsf m}}_{{\mathtt j}, {\mathtt k}})$ is bounded by
${\mathfrak a}_{3,3} \, {\mathtt t}_1^{-d}$.  By Lemma \ref{s10}, we may estimate
the new expression (the previous displayed equation with
$E_{\nu^{\rm gc} _{2,{\mathtt j}, {\textsf M}} } [{\mathfrak p}({\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}}) ]$
replaced by ${\mathfrak p}(\widetilde{{\textsf m}}_{{\mathtt j}, {\mathtt k}})$) with respect
to the grand canonical measure instead of the canonical one at a
multiplicative cost equal to ${\mathfrak a}_1$. At this point, and after a
second order Taylor expansion, the bound \eqref{72} becomes a
straightforward estimate on independent inhomogeneous Bernoulli random
variables.

We next assert that
\begin{align}
\label{71}
\big|\, \widehat{{\mathfrak p}}  ({\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}}) \,\big| \,\le \,
{\mathfrak a}_{3,3} \,\big\{ ( {\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}} - {\textsf m}_{{\mathtt j}, {\mathtt k}}
)^2 \, +\, {\mathtt t}_1^{-d}\,\big\}\,.
\end{align}
To prove this bound, write $\widehat{{\mathfrak p}} ({\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}})$
replacing the expectations with respect to the canonical measures by
expectations with respect to the grand canonical ones:
\begin{align*}
& \widehat{{\mathfrak p}}  ({\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}}) \,=\,
{\mathfrak p}({\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}})  \,-\,
{\mathfrak p}({\textsf m}_{{\mathtt j}, {\mathtt k}}) 
\,-\, {\mathfrak p}'( {\textsf m}_{{\mathtt j},
{\mathtt k}} ) ( {\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}} - {\textsf m}_{{\mathtt j}, {\mathtt k}}   )
\,- \, {\mathfrak R}_n \,
\\
&\quad \text{where}\quad
{\mathfrak R}_n \,=\,
E_{\nu^{\rm c} _{2,{\mathtt j}, {\textsf M}} } [{\mathfrak p}({\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}}) ]
\,-\,  {\mathfrak p}( {\textsf m}_{{\mathtt j}, {\mathtt k}})
\,+\, \big[\,
{\mathfrak p}'( \widetilde{{\textsf m}}_{{\mathtt j}, {\mathtt k}} )
\,-\, {\mathfrak p}'( {\textsf m}_{{\mathtt j}, {\mathtt k}} ) \,\big] \, 
(  {\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}} - {\textsf m}_{{\mathtt j}, {\mathtt k}}   )\,.
\end{align*}
Rewrite the first difference in the definition of ${\mathfrak R}_n$ as the sum of
\begin{align*}
E_{\nu^{\rm c} _{2,{\mathtt j}, {\textsf M}} } [{\mathfrak p}({\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}}) ]
\,-\,  E_{\nu^{\rm gc} _{2,{\mathtt j}, {\textsf M}} } [{\mathfrak p}({\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}}) ]
\,+\,  E_{\nu^{\rm gc} _{2,{\mathtt j}, {\textsf M}} } [{\mathfrak p}({\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}}) ]
\,-\, {\mathfrak p}(\widetilde{{\textsf m}}_{{\mathtt j}, {\mathtt k}}) 
\,+\, {\mathfrak p}(\widetilde{{\textsf m}}_{{\mathtt j}, {\mathtt k}}) 
\,-\, {\mathfrak p}({\textsf m}_{{\mathtt j}, {\mathtt k}}) \,.
\end{align*}
By Lemma \ref{s17}, the absolute value of the first difference is
bounded by ${\mathfrak a}_1 / ({\mathtt t}_1{\mathtt t}_2)^d$. Since ${\mathfrak p}(\cdot)$ and
${\mathfrak p}'(\cdot)$ are Lipschitz continuous on $[0,1]$, the same result
with $p=1$ yields that
$|\, {\mathfrak p}(\widetilde{{\textsf m}}_{{\mathtt j}, {\mathtt k}}) \,-\, {\mathfrak p}({\textsf m}_{{\mathtt j}, {\mathtt k}}) \,| \le {\mathfrak a}_1 / ({\mathtt t}_1{\mathtt t}_2)^d$, and
$|\, {\mathfrak p}'(\widetilde{{\textsf m}}_{{\mathtt j}, {\mathtt k}}) \,-\, {\mathfrak p}'({\textsf m}_{{\mathtt j}, {\mathtt k}}) \,| \le {\mathfrak a}_1 / ({\mathtt t}_1{\mathtt t}_2)^d$.  On the
other hand, by Lemma \ref{s22},
$|\, E_{\nu^{\rm gc} _{2,{\mathtt j}, {\textsf M}} } [{\mathfrak p}({\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}}) ] -
{\mathfrak p}(\widetilde{{\textsf m}}_{{\mathtt j}, {\mathtt k}})| \le {\mathfrak a}_{3,3} / {\mathtt t}_1^d$. To complete the proof of \eqref{71}, apply  a second order
Taylor expansion and Young's inequality $2ab\le a^2 + b^2$.

We turn to the proof of the lemma. Suppose first that
$\beta \, {\mathtt t}_1^{3d}\le 1$. Expand the exponential up to the third
order to obtain that the expectation appearing in the statement of the
lemma is bounded above by
\begin{equation*}
1 \; +\;  \beta \,  E_{\nu^{\rm c} _{2,{\mathtt j}, {\textsf M}} }
\big[ {\mathtt t}_1^d \, \widehat{{\mathfrak p}}  ({\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}}) \big] \;
+\; \beta^2  \, E_{\nu^{\rm c} _{2,{\mathtt j}, {\textsf M}} }
\big[ \big( {\mathtt t}_1^d \, \widehat{{\mathfrak p}}  ({\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}})
 \big)^2 \big]
\; + \; {\mathfrak a}_1\,  \beta^2
\end{equation*}
because $\beta \, {\mathtt t}_1^{3d}\le 1$.  By definition of
$\widehat{{\mathfrak p}} (\cdot)$, the linear term vanishes. By \eqref{72},
the second-order term is bounded by ${\mathfrak a}_{3,3}\, \beta^2 $. To
complete the proof in the case $\beta \, {\mathtt t}_1^{3d}\le 1$, it
remains to recall that $\ln (1+a)\le a$ for all $a>0$.

We turn to the case $\beta \, {\mathtt t}_1^{3d} > 1$.  Fix $\epsilon>0$,
and let ${\color{blue} \kappa } := \epsilon/8$.  We estimate the expectation of
$\exp\{ \beta \, {\mathtt t}_1^d\, \widehat{{\mathfrak p}} ({\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}})\,\}$
according to the value of ${\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}} - {\textsf m}_{{\mathtt j}, {\mathtt k}}$.
We first consider the case in which
$|{\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}} - {\textsf m}_{{\mathtt j}, {\mathtt k}} |\ge {\mathtt t}_1^{-(d/2)+\kappa}$. In this case, the expectation
\begin{equation*}
E_{\nu^{\rm c} _{2,{\mathtt j}, {\textsf M}} } 
\Big[ \, e^{ \beta \, {\mathtt t}_1^d\, \widehat{{\mathfrak p}} ({\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}}) }\,
{\mathtt 1} \big\{ |{\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}} - {\textsf m}_{{\mathtt j}, {\mathtt k}} |\ge 
{\mathtt t}_1^{-(d/2)+\kappa}\,\big\}\, \Big]
\end{equation*}
can be written as the sum of two terms. The first one contains the
values of ${\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}} $ such that
${\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}} - {\textsf m}_{{\mathtt j}, {\mathtt k}} \ge
{\mathtt t}_1^{-(d/2)+\kappa}$, and the second one the values such
that
${\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}} - {\textsf m}_{{\mathtt j}, {\mathtt k}} \le -\,
{\mathtt t}_1^{-(d/2)+\kappa}$. As both terms are estimated similarly, we
consider only the first one which is equal to
\begin{equation*}
\sum_{{\textsf n} \ge {\textsf m}_{{\mathtt j}, {\mathtt k}} +
{\mathtt t}_1^{-(d/2)+\kappa}}
e^{ \beta \, {\mathtt t}_1^d\, \widehat{{\mathfrak p}} ({\textsf n}) }\,
\nu^{\rm c} _{2,{\mathtt j}, {\textsf M}} 
\big\{ {\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}} ={\textsf n} \, \big\}
\,=\,
\sum_{{\textsf N} \ge {\textsf M}_{{\mathtt j}, {\mathtt k}} +
{\mathtt t}_1^{(d/2)+\kappa}}
e^{ \beta \, {\mathtt t}_1^d\, \widehat{{\mathfrak p}} ({\textsf N}/{\mathtt t}^d_1) }\,
\nu^{\rm c} _{2,{\mathtt j}, {\textsf M}} 
\big\{ {\textsf M}_{{\mathtt k}} ={\textsf N} \, \big\} \,.
\end{equation*}
In this formula,
${\textsf M}_{{\mathtt j}, {\mathtt k}} = {\mathtt t}^d_1 \, {\textsf m}_{{\mathtt j}, {\mathtt k}}
$. The first sum is performed over elements ${\textsf n}$ in the set
$\{k/{\mathtt t}^d_1: k\in {\mathbb Z}\}$, while the second one over integers
${\textsf N}$.  Estimate
$\nu^{\rm c} _{2,{\mathtt j}, {\textsf M}} \big\{ {\textsf M}_{{\mathtt k}} ={\textsf N} \,
\big\} $ by
$\nu^{\rm c} _{2,{\mathtt j}, {\textsf M}} \big\{ {\textsf M}_{{\mathtt k}} \ge {\textsf N} \,
\big\} $.  By Corollary \ref{s25}, the previous sum is less than or
equal to
\begin{equation*}
{\mathfrak a}_1\, \sum_{{\textsf N} \ge {\textsf M}_{{\mathtt j}, {\mathtt k}} +
{\mathtt t}_1^{(d/2)+\kappa}}
e^{ \beta \, {\mathtt t}_1^d\, \widehat{{\mathfrak p}} ({\textsf N}/{\mathtt t}^d_1) }\,
e^{ - (1/2) ( {\textsf N} - {\textsf M}_{{\mathtt j}, {\mathtt k}})^2 {\mathtt t}_1^{-d}}\,.
\end{equation*}
Since $\beta \le 1/(4\, {\mathfrak a}_{3,3})$, by \eqref{71} and elementary
Gaussian bounds, this expression is less than or equal to
${\mathfrak a}_{3,3}\, \exp\{-\, (1/4) \, {\mathtt t}_1^ {2\kappa} \}$ for
${\mathtt t}_1 \ge 2$. Therefore,
\begin{align}
\label{177}
E_{\nu^{\rm c} _{2,{\mathtt j}, {\textsf M}} } 
\Big[ \, e^{ \beta \, {\mathtt t}_1^d\, \widehat{{\mathfrak p}} ({\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}}) }\,
{\mathtt 1} \big\{ |{\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}} - {\textsf m}_{{\mathtt j}, {\mathtt k}} |\ge 
{\mathtt t}_1^{-(d/2)+\kappa}\,\big\}\, \Big]
\,\le\, {\mathfrak a}_{3,3}\, C_0(\kappa)\, e^{-\, {\mathtt t}_1^ {2\kappa} /4}\,.
\end{align}

We turn to the case
$|{\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}} - {\textsf m}_{{\mathtt j}, {\mathtt k}} |\le {\mathtt t}_1^{-(d/2)+\kappa}$.  By \eqref{71} and since, by hypothesis
$\beta\le {\mathtt t}_1^{-8\kappa}$, in this region there exists a constant
${\mathfrak a}_{3,3}$ such that
\begin{equation*}
\beta \, {\mathtt t}_1^d \, \widehat{ {\mathfrak p}} ({\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}}) \,
\le \; {\mathfrak a}_{3,3}\,  \beta \, {\mathtt t}_1^{2\kappa} 
\; <\;  {\mathfrak a}_{3,3}\, {\mathtt t}_1^{-6\kappa} \quad\text{and}\quad
\big\{\, \beta \,{\mathtt t}_1^d \, \widehat{ {\mathfrak p}}
({\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}})  \, \big\}^3 \; 
\le \; {\mathfrak a}_{3,3}\,  \beta^3 \, {\mathtt t}_1^{6\kappa} \; <\;
{\mathfrak a}_{3,3} \,  \beta^2 \,  {\mathtt t}_1^{-2\kappa}\,.
\end{equation*}
Expanding the exponential up to third order yields that
\begin{align*}
& E_{\nu^{\rm c} _{2,{\mathtt j}, {\textsf M}} } 
\Big[ \, e^{ \beta \, {\mathtt t}_1^d\, \widehat{{\mathfrak p}} ({\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}}) }\,
{\mathtt 1} \big\{ |{\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}} - {\textsf m}_{{\mathtt j}, {\mathtt k}} |\le 
{\mathtt t}_1^{-(d/2)+\kappa}\,\big\}\, \Big]
\\
&\quad \,\le\,
1 \; +\;  E_{\nu^{\rm c} _{2,{\mathtt j}, {\textsf M}}}
\big[ \, \beta \, {\mathtt t}_1^d \, \widehat{ {\mathfrak p}} ({\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}}) \,
{\mathtt 1} \big \{ | {\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}} - {\textsf m}_{{\mathtt j}, {\mathtt k}} |
\, \le\,  {\mathtt t}_1^{-(d/2)+\kappa}\big\}\big] 
\, +\; \beta^2  \,
E_{\nu^{\rm c} _{2,{\mathtt j}, {\textsf M}}} \big[ \, \big( 
{\mathtt t}_1^d \, \widehat{ {\mathfrak p}} ({\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}})  \big)^2 \big]
\; + \; {\mathfrak a}_{3,3}  \, \beta^2  \, {\mathtt t}_1^{- 2 \kappa}\; .
\end{align*}

We may rewrite the first order term as
\begin{align*}
E_{\nu^{\rm c} _{2,{\mathtt j}, {\textsf M}}}
\big[ \, \beta \, {\mathtt t}_1^d \, \widehat{ {\mathfrak p}} ({\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}}) \, \big] 
\,-\,
E_{\nu^{\rm c} _{2,{\mathtt j}, {\textsf M}}}
\big[ \, \beta \, {\mathtt t}_1^d \, \widehat{ {\mathfrak p}} ({\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}}) \,
{\mathtt 1} \big \{ | {\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}} - {\textsf m}_{{\mathtt j}, {\mathtt k}} |
\, > \,  {\mathtt t}_1^{-(d/2)+\kappa}\big\}\big] 
\; .
\end{align*}
The first expectation vanishes by definition of
$\widehat{ {\mathfrak p}} (\cdot)$. By Corollary \ref{s25}, as $\beta \le 1$
and $\widehat{ {\mathfrak p}} (\cdot)$ is bounded, the second expectation is
bounded by
${\mathfrak a}_1\, C_0(\kappa)\, \exp\{ - (1/4) {\mathtt t}_1^{2\kappa}\}$.  On
the other hand, by \eqref{72}, the second order term in the
penultimate displayed equation is bounded by ${\mathfrak a}_{3,3}\,
\beta^2$. Therefore, 
\begin{align*}
E_{\nu^{\rm c} _{2,{\mathtt j}, {\textsf M}} } 
\Big[ \, e^{ \beta \, {\mathtt t}_1^d\, \widehat{{\mathfrak p}} ({\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}}) }\,
{\mathtt 1} \big\{ |{\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}} - {\textsf m}_{{\mathtt j}, {\mathtt k}} |\le 
{\mathtt t}_1^{-(d/2)+\kappa}\,\big\}\, \Big]
\,\le\, 1\,+\, 
{\mathfrak a}_1 \, C_0(\kappa)\, e^{ - {\mathtt t}_1^{2\kappa}/4}
\; +\; {\mathfrak a}_{3,3}\, \beta^2\,.
\end{align*}
This expression is less than or equal to
$1 + {\mathfrak a}_{3,3}\, C_0(\kappa) \, \beta^2$ for all ${\mathtt t}_1\ge 2$
because $\beta^{-1} <{\mathtt t}_1^{3d}$.  To complete the proof of the
lemma in the case $\beta \, {\mathtt t}_1^{3d} > 1$, it remains to recall
that $\ln (1+u)\le u$, and to sum the previous estimate with the one
obtained in \eqref{177}.
<!-- end proof-19 -->
<!-- corollary-6: body_md -->
\label{s27}
Fix a polynomial ${\mathfrak p}(\cdot)$, a continuous function
$J\colon {\mathbb T}^d \to {\mathbb R}$, and $\epsilon>0$.  Then, there exists a
finite constant ${\mathfrak a}_{3,3} = {\mathfrak a}_{3,3}(\epsilon, {\mathfrak p})$, such
that
\begin{equation*}
\sum_{{\mathtt j} \in \Sigma^+_{{\mathtt t}_3}}
\int {\mathtt 1}\{ {\textsf m}_{2, {\mathtt j}} \in ({\mathfrak r}_- , {\mathfrak r}_+) \}
\,  \sum_{{\mathtt k} \in \Lambda_{{\mathtt j}}} {\mathtt t}^d_1\, J_{{\mathtt k}}\,
 \widehat{ {\mathfrak p}} ({\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}})  \, f\;
d\nu^n_{\rho(\cdot)}
\,\le\,
\delta\, n^2\, I_n (f\,;\, \nu^n_{\rho(\cdot)})
\,+\, \frac{{\mathfrak a}_{3,3}}{\delta} \, \Vert J\Vert^2_{\infty}\,
{\mathtt t}_2^{2d}  \, \Big( \frac{n}{{\mathtt t}_1 {\mathtt t}_2}\Big)^{d-2} 
\end{equation*}
for all $\delta>0$, integers ${\mathtt t}_1\ge 2$, ${\mathtt t}_2\ge 2$ such
that
${\mathtt t}_2^{2+d} \le (\delta / {\mathfrak c}_{\rm LS}) \Vert J\Vert_\infty^{-1}\,
(n/{\mathtt t}_1)^2 \, ({\mathfrak b}_1 \wedge {\mathtt t}_1^{-\epsilon})$, and
densities $f$ with respect to $\nu^n_{\rho(\cdot)}$.
<!-- end corollary-6 -->
<!-- proof-20: body_md -->
Repeat Steps 1 and 2 in the proof of Lemma \ref{s23} to project on
the hyperplanes
${\color{blue} \Omega_{2,{\mathtt j}, {\textsf M}}} := \{\eta \in
\{0,1\}^{B_{2,{\mathtt j}}} : \sum_{x\in B_{2,{\mathtt j}}} \eta_x =
{\textsf M}\}$. These projections yield that the left-hand side of the
expression in the statement of the corollary is equal to
\begin{equation}
\label{04c}
\begin{gathered}
\sum_{{\mathtt j} \in \Sigma^+_{{\mathtt t}_3}} \sum_{{\textsf M} }
\nu^{2, {\mathtt j}}_{\rho (\cdot)}  (\Omega_{2,{\mathtt j}, {\textsf M}})\,
\< f_{2,{\mathtt j}}  \>_{2,{\mathtt j} , {\textsf M}} \,
\int W_{{\mathtt j}}  \, f^{({\textsf M})}_{2,{\mathtt j}} \, d\nu^{\rm c}_{2, {\mathtt j}, {\textsf M}}
\;,
\\
\text{where}\quad
{\color{blue} W_{{\mathtt j}} } :=\sum_{{\mathtt k} \in \Lambda_{{\mathtt j}}} J_{{\mathtt k}}\,
{\mathtt t}^d_1\; \widehat{ {\mathfrak p}} ({\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}}) \,, \quad 
{\mathtt j} \in \Sigma^+_{{\mathtt t}_3}\,,
\end{gathered}
\end{equation}
and the sum over ${\textsf M}$ is carried over integers ${\textsf M}$ such that
${\mathfrak r}_- \le {\textsf M}/ | B_{2, {\mathtt j}} | \le {\mathfrak r}_+$. By the
entropy inequality, this expression is less than or equal to
\begin{equation*}
\sum_{{\mathtt j} \in \Sigma^+_{{\mathtt t}_3}} \sum_{{\textsf M} }
\nu^{2, {\mathtt j}}_{\rho (\cdot)}  (\Omega_{2, {\mathtt j}, {\textsf M}})\,
\< f_{2,{\mathtt j}}  \>_{2,{\mathtt j} , {\textsf M}} \,
\Big\{ \, \frac{1}{\gamma}\,
H  ( f^{({\textsf M})}_{2,{\mathtt j}}  \,|\,  \nu^{\rm c}_{2, {\mathtt j}, {\textsf M}})
\,+\, \frac{1}{\gamma}\, \ln
\int e^{\gamma W_{{\mathtt j}} }  \, d\nu^{\rm c}_{2, {\mathtt j}, {\textsf M}}\, \Big\}
\end{equation*}
for all $\gamma>0$. Let ${\color{blue} L} = {\mathtt t}_1{\mathtt t}_2$. By the logarithmic
Sobolev inequality, the first term is bounded by
\begin{equation*}
\sum_{{\mathtt j} \in \Sigma^+_{{\mathtt t}_3}} \sum_{{\textsf M} }
\nu^{2, {\mathtt j}}_{\rho (\cdot)}  (\Omega_{2, {\mathtt j}, {\textsf M}})\,
\< f_{2,{\mathtt j}}  \>_{2,{\mathtt j} , {\textsf M}} \,
\frac{1}{\gamma}\, {\mathfrak c}_{\rm LS} \, L^2\, 
I_{B_{2, {\mathtt j}} }   ( f^{({\textsf M})}_{2,{\mathtt j}}
\,;\,  \nu^{\rm c}_{2, {\mathtt j}, {\textsf M}})
\;\le\;
\frac{1}{\gamma}\, {\mathfrak c}_{\rm LS} \, L^2\, 
I_{n}   ( f \,;\,  \nu^n_{\rho(\cdot)})\,.
\end{equation*}
Set $\gamma = {\mathfrak c}_{\rm LS} \, \delta^{-1}\, (L/n)^2$ to obtain the
first term on the right-hand side of the statement of the corollary.

By H\"older's inequality the second term in the next to last equation
is bounded by
\begin{equation*}
\sum_{{\mathtt j} \in \Sigma^+_{{\mathtt t}_3}} \sum_{{\textsf M} }
\nu^{2, {\mathtt j}}_{\rho (\cdot)}  (\Omega_{2, {\mathtt j}, {\textsf M}})\,
\< f_{2,{\mathtt j}}  \>_{2,{\mathtt j} , {\textsf M}} \,
\Big\{ \, \frac{1}{\gamma}\, \frac{1}{{\mathtt t}_2^d }\,
\sum_{{\mathtt k} \in \Lambda_{{\mathtt j}}}   \ln
\int
e^{\gamma J_{{\mathtt k}}\, {\mathtt t}_2^d\, {\mathtt t}^d_1\; \widehat{ {\mathfrak p}} ({\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}})   }
\, d\nu^{\rm c}_{2, {\mathtt j}, {\textsf M}}\, \Big\}\,.
\end{equation*}
By hypothesis,
$\gamma \, |J_{{\mathtt k}}|\, {\mathtt t}_2^d \le {\mathfrak b}_1 \wedge {\mathtt t}_1^{-\epsilon}$. We may therefore apply Lemma \ref{s16}, which
asserts that the previous expression is less than or equal to
\begin{equation*}
{\mathfrak a}_{3,3} (\epsilon, {\mathfrak p}) \,
\sum_{{\mathtt j} \in \Sigma^+_{{\mathtt t}_3}} \sum_{{\textsf M} }
\nu^{2, {\mathtt j}}_{\rho (\cdot)}  (\Omega_{2, {\mathtt j}, {\textsf M}})\,
\< f_{2,{\mathtt j}}  \>_{2,{\mathtt j} , {\textsf M}} \,
\gamma\,  J_{{\mathtt k}}^2\, {\mathtt t}_2^{2d}
\,\le\,
{\mathfrak a}_{3,3} (\epsilon, {\mathfrak p}) \,
\Vert J\Vert_\infty^2\, \gamma\, n^d \,
\Big(\frac{{\mathtt t}_2}{{\mathtt t}_1}\Big)^d 
\,,
\end{equation*}
which completes the proof of the corollary.
<!-- end proof-20 -->
<!-- lemma-15: body_md -->
\label{s28}
Fix a polynomial ${\mathfrak p}(\cdot)$, a function
$J\colon {\mathbb T}^d \to {\mathbb R}$ of class $C^1$, $\delta>0$, and $K_1\ge 1$.
Then, there exist finite constants ${\mathfrak a}_{3,1}$, $C_0 = C_0({\mathfrak p})$
such that
\begin{equation*} 
\sum_{{\mathtt j}\in \Sigma^+_{{\mathtt t}_3 }} 
\int  {\mathtt 1}\{ {\textsf m}_{2, {\mathtt j}} \in ({\mathfrak r}_- ,\, {\mathfrak r}_+) \}
\sum_{{\mathtt k}\in \Lambda_{{\mathtt j}}} {\mathtt t}^d_1 \,  
J_{{\mathtt k}}  \, V_{{\mathtt j}, {\mathtt k}} \, f \, d  \nu^n_{\rho(\cdot)} \,\le\,
\delta\, n^2 \,  I_n  ( f \,;\, \nu^n_{\rho (\cdot)} ) \,+\,
{\mathfrak a}_{3,1} \, \frac{{\mathfrak c}_{\rm LS}}{\delta} \,
{\mathfrak C}_2 \, \Big(\frac{{\mathtt t}_1{\mathtt t}_2}{n}\Big)^4\, n^d  
\end{equation*}
for all densities $f$ with respect to $\nu^n_{\rho(\cdot)}$, and
${\mathtt t}_1\ge 2$, ${\mathtt t}_2\ge 2$ such that
$({\mathtt t}_1{\mathtt t}_2)^{d+3} \le K_1\, n^3$. In this equation, ${\mathfrak C}_2 =
\exp\{ {\mathfrak c}_{\rm LS} C_0({\mathfrak p})\, K_1 \, (\, {\mathfrak a}_{3,1} + \Vert
J\Vert_{C^1})/\delta\}$.
<!-- end lemma-15 -->
<!-- proof-21: body_md -->
Rewrite the sum over ${\mathtt k}$ on the left-hand side as
\begin{equation}
\label{70}
\begin{aligned}
\sum_{{\mathtt k}\in \Lambda_{{\mathtt j}}} {\mathtt t}^d_1 \,  
J_{{\mathtt k}}  V_{{\mathtt j}, {\mathtt k}}
\, & =\, 
\sum_{{\mathtt k}\in \Lambda_{{\mathtt j}}} {\mathtt t}^d_1 \,  
[\, J_{{\mathtt k}}  -  \, J_{2, {\mathtt j}}  \,]
\,  {\mathfrak p}'( \widetilde{{\textsf m}}_{{\mathtt j}, {\mathtt k}} ) \,
( {\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}} - {\textsf m}_{{\mathtt j}, {\mathtt k}} )
\\
\, & +\, 
{\mathtt t}^d_1 \,  J_{2, {\mathtt j}} 
\sum_{{\mathtt k}\in \Lambda_{{\mathtt j}}}
[\, {\mathfrak p}'( \widetilde{{\textsf m}}_{{\mathtt j}, {\mathtt k}} )
- {\mathfrak p}'( {\textsf m}_{2, {\mathtt j}}   )\,] \, 
( {\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}} -
{\textsf m}_{{\mathtt j}, {\mathtt k}} ) \,,
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
where
${\color{blue}  J_{2, {\mathtt j}} } = {\mathtt t}_2^{-d} \sum_{{\mathtt k}\in \Lambda_{{\mathtt j}}} J_{{\mathtt k}}$. In the last identity we used the fact that
\begin{equation*}
\sum_{{\mathtt k}\in \Lambda_{{\mathtt j}}} {\mathfrak p}'( {\textsf m}_{2, {\mathtt j}}   )\, 
( {\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}} - {\textsf m}_{{\mathtt j}, {\mathtt k}} ) \,=\, 0 
\end{equation*}
for all ${\mathtt j}\in \Sigma^+_{{\mathtt t}_3}$ because, by definition of ${\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}} $ and ${\textsf m}_{{\mathtt j}, {\mathtt k}}$,
\begin{align*}
\sum_{{\mathtt k}\in \Lambda_{{\mathtt j}}}  {\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}} \,=\, 
\sum_{{\mathtt k}\in \Lambda_{{\mathtt j}}}  \frac{1}{|B_{{\mathtt k}}|}
\sum_{x\in B_{{\mathtt k}}} \eta_x \,=\, \frac{1}{|B_{{\mathtt k}}|} \,
{\textsf M}_{2, {\mathtt j}}
\,=\, \sum_{{\mathtt k}\in \Lambda_{{\mathtt j}}}  {\textsf m}_{{\mathtt j}, {\mathtt k}}\,.
\end{align*}

Now, Lemma \ref{s23} provides bounds for the terms \eqref{70}.  Let
\begin{equation*}
V_{{\mathtt j}} \,=\, {\mathtt 1}\{ {\textsf m}_{2, {\mathtt j}} \in ({\mathfrak r}_- , {\mathfrak r}_+) \}
\sum_{{\mathtt k}\in \Lambda_{{\mathtt j}}} {\mathtt t}^d_1 \,  
[\, J_{{\mathtt k}}  -  \, J_{2, {\mathtt j}}  \,]
\,  {\mathfrak p}'( \widetilde{{\textsf m}}_{{\mathtt j}, {\mathtt k}} ) \,
( {\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}} - {\textsf m}_{{\mathtt j}, {\mathtt k}} )\,, \qquad
{\mathtt j}\in \Sigma^+_{{\mathtt t}_3} \,.
\end{equation*}
Clearly,
$\Vert V_{{\mathtt j}} \Vert_\infty \le C_0({\mathfrak p}) \, \Vert J \Vert_{C^1}\,
({\mathtt t}_1{\mathtt t}_2)^d \, ({\mathtt t}_1{\mathtt t}_2/n)$. Since, by hypothesis,
$({\mathtt t}_1{\mathtt t}_2)^{d+3} \le K_1 \, n^3$,
$\Vert V_{{\mathtt j}} \Vert_\infty \le C_1 \, (n/{\mathtt t}_1{\mathtt t}_2)^2$, where
${\color{blue} C_1} := C_0({\mathfrak p}) \, K_1\, \Vert J \Vert_{C^1}\,$. Thus, each
function $V_{{\mathtt j}} $ satisfies the assumptions of Lemma \ref{s23}
with $r_1 = {\mathtt t}_1 {\mathtt t}_2$, $r_2={\mathtt t}_3$.  Therefore, by this
result,
\begin{equation*}
\sum_{{\mathtt j}\in \Sigma^+_{{\mathtt t}_3 }} 
\int V_{{\mathtt j}}  \, f \, d  \nu^n_{\rho(\cdot)} \,\le\,
\delta\, n^2 \,  I_n  ( f \,;\, \nu^n_{\rho (\cdot)} ) \,+\,
C_2\, \Big(\frac{{\mathtt t}_1{\mathtt t}_2}{n}\Big)^2\,
\sum_{{\mathtt j}\in \Sigma^+_{{\mathtt t}_3}} 
\max_{{\mathfrak r}_- \le {\textsf m} \le {\mathfrak r}_+} \int V^2_{{\mathtt j}} \;
d\nu^{\rm c}_{ 2, {\mathtt j}, {\textsf M}} 
\end{equation*}
for all densities $f$ with respect to $\nu^n_{\rho(\cdot)}$.  The
maximum over densities ${\textsf m}$ is carried on the interval
$({\mathfrak r}_- ,\, {\mathfrak r}_+)$ because $V_{{\mathtt j}} $ vanishes outside it, and
${\color{blue}  C_2} := ({\mathfrak c}_{\rm LS} / 2 \delta)\, \exp\{C_1 {\mathfrak c}_{\rm LS}
/\delta\}$, where $C_1$ has been introduced above in the proof and
${\mathfrak c}_{\rm LS}$ is the logarithmic Sobolev constant.

We estimate the remaining integral. As $J$ is of class $C^1$,
$|\, J_{{\mathtt k}} - \, J_{2, {\mathtt j}} \,|\le \Vert J\Vert_{C^1} \, ({\mathtt t}_1{\mathtt t}_2/n)$. Hence, by Corollary \ref{s71},
\begin{equation*}
\max_{{\mathfrak r}_-  \le {\textsf m} \le {\mathfrak r}_+} \int V^2_{{\mathtt j}}\;
d\nu^{\rm c}_{ 2, {\mathtt j}, {\textsf M}}
\,\le\,
{\mathfrak a}_1  \, \Vert J\Vert^2_{C^1}
\, ({\mathtt t}_1 \,{\mathtt t}_2)^d\, ({\mathtt t}_1{\mathtt t}_2/n)^2
\quad \text{for all}\;\; {\mathtt j}\in \Sigma^+_{{\mathtt t}_3} \,.
\end{equation*}

To complete the proof of the estimate for the first term in
\eqref{70}, it remains to recollect all previous bounds, noting the
overestimate $\|J\|^2_{C^1} \le 2 \, \exp\{\|J\|_{C^1}\}$.

The same argument applies to the second term in \eqref{70} because, by
\eqref{57},
$|\widetilde{{\textsf m}}_{{\mathtt j}, {\mathtt k}} - {\textsf m}_{2, {\mathtt j}}|\le {\mathfrak a}_{3,1} \, ({\mathtt t}_1 {\mathtt t}_2/n)$. Thus, in the previous argument the
estimate
$|\, J_{{\mathtt k}} - \, J_{2, {\mathtt j}} \,|\le \Vert J\Vert_{C^1} \, ({\mathtt t}_1{\mathtt t}_2/n)$ is replaced by the previous one, and we get the same
bounds with ${\mathfrak a}_{3,1}$ in place of $\Vert J\Vert_{C^1}$.
<!-- end proof-21 -->
<!-- proof-22: body_md -->
It follows from Corollary \ref{s27} and Lemma \ref{s28}.
<!-- end proof-22 -->
<!-- proposition-4: body_md -->
\label{s44}
Fix $p\ge 1$, a function $J\colon {\mathbb T}^d \to {\mathbb R}$ of class $C^1$,
and constants $K_1\ge 1$, $K_2\ge 1$.  Then, there exist finite
constants ${\mathfrak a}_1$, ${\mathfrak a}_{3,3} = {\mathfrak a}_{3,3}(p)$, $C_2= C_2(p)$
such that
\begin{equation*}
\begin{aligned}
&\int \Big |\,
\sum_{{\mathtt j} \in \Sigma^+_{{\mathtt t}_3}}
{\mathtt 1}\{ {\textsf m}_{2, {\mathtt j}} \in ({\mathfrak r}_- , {\mathfrak r}_+) \}
\, {\mathfrak W}_{p, J} ({\textsf m}_{2, {\mathtt j}}) \,\Big |\, 
f\, d\nu^n_{\rho(\cdot)}
\\
&\quad 
\,\le\, {\mathfrak a}_{3,3}\,  \, \Vert J\Vert_{\infty} n^d\, \Big\{ \, \Big(
\frac{{\mathtt t}_1{\mathtt t}_2 }{n} \Big)^4
\,+\,  \frac{{\mathtt t}_1{\mathtt t}_2 }{n} \, \frac{1} {({\mathtt t}_1{\mathtt t}_2)^d } \, 
\,+\,  \frac{1 }{{\mathtt t}_1^{d}}   \, \Big[ \, 
\frac{1 }{{\mathtt t}_1^{2d}} \,+\, \frac{1 }{({\mathtt t}_1{\mathtt t}_2)^{d}} \,+\,
\Big(\frac{{\mathtt t}_1 }{n} \Big)^2\,\Big] \Big\}
\\
&\quad
\,+\, 
{\mathfrak a}_{3,3} \, \Vert J\Vert_{C^1}
\,\Big\{   \, H_n (f\,|\, \nu^n_{\rho(\cdot)})\, + \, \ln(2)\,\Big\}
\,+\, {\mathfrak a}_1 \, \Vert J\Vert_{\infty}\,
\Big( \frac{n}{{\mathtt t}_1{\mathtt t}_2}\Big)^d\,
e^{- ({\mathtt t}_1{\mathtt t}_2)^d/{\mathfrak a}_1}
\\
&\quad
\,+\, {\mathfrak a}_{3,3}\, \, \Vert J\Vert_{C^1}\, \Big\{
\Big( \frac{{\mathtt t}_1{\mathtt t}_2}{n}\Big)^2\, 
\Big( \frac{n}{ ({\mathtt t}_1{\mathtt t}_2)^{1/2}} \Big)^d
\,+\,   \Big[\, e^{C_2 K_2^d}\,
+ e^{{\mathfrak a}_{3,3} K_1}\, ({\mathtt t}_1{\mathtt t}_2)^{2d}\,
\Big( \frac{{\mathtt t}_1{\mathtt t}_2}{n}\Big)^6
\,\Big] \, 
\Big( \frac{n}{ ({\mathtt t}_1{\mathtt t}_2)^{2}} \Big)^d \, \Big\}
\end{aligned}
\end{equation*}
for all integers ${\mathtt t}_1\ge 2$, ${\mathtt t}_2\ge 2$ such that
$({\mathtt t}_1{\mathtt t}_2)^{d+3} \le K_1\, n^3$,
$ ({\mathtt t}_1{\mathtt t}_2)^{1+(d/4)} \le n$, ${\mathtt t}_2 \le K_2\, {\mathtt t}_1$,
and densities $f$ with respect to $\nu^n_{\rho(\cdot)}$.
<!-- end proposition-4 -->
<!-- remark-22: body_md -->
\label{rm6}
One would wish to replace
$\sum_{{\mathtt k} \in \Lambda_{{\mathtt j}}} {\mathtt t}_1^d\, J_{{\mathtt k}}\, {\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}}^p$ by $({\mathtt t}_1{\mathtt t}_2)^d\, J_{2,{\mathtt j}}\, {\textsf m}_{2,{\mathtt j}}^p $. The
previous result states that such a replacement carries a correction
which arises from replacing expectations with respect to
canonical measures by expectations with respect to grand canonical
measures.
<!-- end remark-22 -->
<!-- proof-23: body_md -->
We first remove the indicator
${\mathtt 1}\{{\textsf m}_{2, {\mathtt j}} \in ({\mathfrak r}_- , {\mathfrak r}_+) \}$ applying Lemma
\ref{s07b} with $r_1 = {\mathtt t}_1{\mathtt t}_2$. This explains the presence
of the term
${\mathfrak a}_1 \, ( n/{\mathtt t}_1{\mathtt t}_2)^d\, \exp\{- ({\mathtt t}_1{\mathtt t}_2)^d/{\mathfrak a}_1\}$ on the right-hand side.

The proof relies on Lemma \ref{s32} and Corollary \ref{s30b}. Lemma
\ref{s32} requires subtracting the expectation of the integrand $F$ with
respect to $\nu^n_{\rho(\cdot)}$. To guarantee the presence of this
expectation, write
\begin{equation*}
E_{\nu^n_{\rho(\cdot)}} [{\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}}^p] \,=\,
E_{\nu^n_{\rho(\cdot)}} \Big[ E_{\nu^n_{\rho(\cdot)}}
\big[\, {\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}}^p \,|\, {\textsf M}_{2,{\mathtt j}}\,\big]\, \Big] \,=\,
E_{\nu^n_{\rho(\cdot)}} \Big[ E_{\nu^{\rm c}_{2, {\mathtt j}, {\textsf M}}}
\big[\, {\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}}^p \,\big]\, \Big] \quad
\text{for}\;\; {\mathtt k}\in \Lambda_{{\mathtt j}} \,.
\end{equation*}
Every operation carried out on
$E_{\nu^{\rm c}_{{\textsf 2}, {\mathtt j}, M}} [{\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}}^p]$ is also applied to
the last term of the previous displayed equation. For example, to
estimate the sum appearing in the statement of the proposition we expand
the sum
$\sum_{{\mathtt k} \in \Lambda_{{\mathtt j}}} J_{{\mathtt k}}\, E_{\nu^{\rm c}_{{\textsf 2},
{\mathtt j}, M}} [{\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}}^p]$ applying Corollary \ref{s30b}. The
same expansion is performed to the corresponding term
$\sum_{{\mathtt k} \in \Lambda_{{\mathtt j}}} J_{{\mathtt k}}\,
E_{\nu^n_{\rho(\cdot)}} [ \, E_{\nu^{\rm c}_{2, {\mathtt j}, {\textsf M}}} \big[\, {\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}}^p \,\big] \,]$ without explicitly mentioning it.

Corollary \ref{s30b} expresses
$\sum_{{\mathtt k} \in \Lambda_{{\mathtt j}}} J_{{\mathtt k}}\, E_{\nu^{\rm c}_{{\textsf 2},
{\mathtt j}, M}} [{\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}}^p]$ as the sum of five terms and a
remainder. Note that we have an extra multiplicative factor
${\mathtt t}^d_1$ in comparison with Corollary \ref{s30b}.  The terms
inside the brace in the first line on the right-hand side of the
inequality stated in the proposition correspond to the bound on the
remainder obtained in Corollary \ref{s30b}.

To complete the proof, we have to show that the expectation with
respect to the measure $ f\; d\nu^n_{\rho (\cdot)} $ of the terms
which appear in Corollary \ref{s30b} and do not appear in the
statement of Proposition \ref{s44} can be estimated by the entropy
$H_n(f \,|\, \nu^n_{\rho (\cdot)})$ and small constants.

We start with the last term in \eqref{110}. Let
$F(a) = \chi(a) \, a^{p-2}$.  By Lemma \ref{s32} with
$r_1 = {\mathtt t}_1{\mathtt t}_2$, ${\mathfrak a} ({\mathtt i}) =J_{2, {\mathtt i}}$ and
$\gamma^{-1} = \Vert J\Vert_\infty$, there exists a finite constant
$C$, depending only on $p$, such that
\begin{equation}
\label{100}
\begin{aligned}
& \int\Big |  \sum_{{\mathtt j}\in \Sigma^+_{{\mathtt t}_3}}
J_{2, {\mathtt j}}\,
\big[ \, F({\textsf m}_{2,{\mathtt j}}) - E_{\nu^n_{\rho (\cdot)}} [F({\textsf m}_{2, {\mathtt j}}) ] \, \big] 
\,  \Big| \, f\; d\nu^n_{\rho (\cdot)}
\\
&\quad
\,\le \, \Vert J\Vert_\infty  \, \Big\{   \, H_n(f \,|\, \nu^n_{\rho (\cdot)}  )
\,+\,\ln(2) \,+\,  C(p)\, 
\Big( \frac{n}{({\mathtt t}_1{\mathtt t}_2)^{2}} \Big)^d\, \Big\}\,.
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
This estimate provides a bound for the expectation with respect to
the measure $ f\; d\nu^n_{\rho (\cdot)} $ of the last term in
\eqref{110} multiplied by ${\mathtt t}_1^d$. Below, we will simply say that
it provides an estimate for the $i$-th term in \eqref{110}, omitting that
it is in reality an estimate for the expectation of the expression
multiplied by ${\mathtt t}_1^d$. Mind also that, without mentioning it, we
are subtracting the mean of the term with respect to
$\nu^n_{\rho (\cdot)}$.

The same argument applies to all terms of order
$({\mathtt t}_1{\mathtt t}_2/n)^3$.  By definition, see Lemma \ref{s20b},
$[H^{(1)}_{{\mathtt j}, {\mathtt k}}]^3$,
$H^{(1)}_{{\mathtt j}, {\mathtt k}} \, {\mathtt Y}^{(2)}_{{\mathtt j}, {\mathtt k}}$ and
$ [\, J_{{\mathtt k}} - J_{2, {\mathtt j}}\,] \, {\mathtt Y}^{(2)}_{{\mathtt j}, {\mathtt k}} $
are of order $({\mathtt t}_1{\mathtt t}_2/n)^3$. More precisely, since by
hypothesis $({\mathtt t}_1{\mathtt t}_2)^{d+3} \le K_1\, n^3$, Lemma \ref{s32}
with $r_1 = {\mathtt t}_1{\mathtt t}_2$,
${\mathfrak a} ({\mathtt j}) = {\mathtt t}_1^d \sum_{{\mathtt k} \in \Lambda_{{\mathtt j}}} J_{{\mathtt k}} \,
[H^{(1)}_{{\mathtt j}, {\mathtt k}} ]^3$ and
$F(x) = (1/6) \, Q_p'''(x) \, \chi(x)^3$ provides a bound for the
fourth term on the right-hand side of \eqref{110} similar to
\eqref{100}. On the right-hand side of the inequality, instead of the
expression which appears in \eqref{100}, we have
\begin{equation}
\label{101}
\Vert J \Vert_\infty  \, \Big\{   \, H_n(f \,|\, \nu^n_{\rho (\cdot)}
)  \,+\, \ln (2) \,+\, {\mathfrak a}_{3,1} (p)\, e^{{\mathfrak a}_{3,1} (p) \, K_1}\,
({\mathtt t}_1{\mathtt t}_2)^{2d}\, \Big( \frac{{\mathtt t}_1{\mathtt t}_2}{n}\Big)^6\, 
\Big( \frac{n}{({\mathtt t}_1{\mathtt t}_2)^{2}} \Big)^d\, \Big\}\,.
\end{equation}
As $K_1\ge 1$,
${\mathfrak a}_{3,1} (p)\, e^{{\mathfrak a}_{3,1} (p) \, K_1} \le e^{2 {\mathfrak a}_{3,1}
(p) \, K_1}$, and we can get rid of the multiplicative constant.

An identical bound is obtained for the sums involving
$H^{(1)}_{{\mathtt j}, {\mathtt k}} \, {\mathtt Y}^{(2)}_{{\mathtt j}, {\mathtt k}}$ and
$ [\, J_{{\mathtt k}} - J_{2, {\mathtt j}}\,] \, {\mathtt Y}^{(2)}_{{\mathtt j}, {\mathtt k}}$.
Some of these terms are multiplied by polynomials of ${\textsf m}_{2,{\mathtt j}}$. This does not interfere in the argument since we are always
subtracting the expectations with respect to $\nu^n_{\rho(\cdot)}$.
In the estimate of the term $[\, J_{{\mathtt k}} - J_{2, {\mathtt j}}\,] \,
{\mathtt Y}^{(2)}_{{\mathtt j}, {\mathtt k}}$, we get the $C^1$ norm of $J$ instead
of the $L^\infty$ one, and a constant of type ${\mathfrak a}_{3,2}$ instead of
${\mathfrak a}_{3,1}$ because of the Hessian of $\rho$ in the term $H^{(4)}$.

Since
${\mathtt Y}_{{\mathtt j}, {\mathtt k}} = H^{(1)}_{{\mathtt j}, {\mathtt k}} + {\mathtt Y}^{(2)}_{{\mathtt j}, {\mathtt k}}$, it remains to estimate
\begin{equation}
\label{102b}
\begin{aligned}
& {\mathtt t}_2^d\, J_{2,{\mathtt j}}\, {\textsf Q}_p({\textsf m}_{2,{\mathtt j}})
\,+\, {\textsf Q}'_p({\textsf m}_{2,{\mathtt j}}) \,
\chi ({\textsf m}_{2,{\mathtt j}})\,
\sum_{{\mathtt k}\in\Lambda_{{\mathtt j}}}  [\, J_{{\mathtt k}} - J_{2, {\mathtt j}}\,] \,
H^{(1)}_{{\mathtt j}, {\mathtt k}}  \\
& +\, \frac{1}{2}\, {\textsf Q}''_p({\textsf m}_{2,{\mathtt j}}) \,
\chi({\textsf m}_{2,{\mathtt j}})^2\,  \sum_{{\mathtt k}\in\Lambda_{{\mathtt j}}}  J_{{\mathtt k}} \,
[H^{(1)}_{{\mathtt j}, {\mathtt k}} ]^2 \,.
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
Recall the definition of ${\textsf Q}_p(\cdot)$ introduced in \eqref{99}.
We claim that the second and third terms in \eqref{102b} with
${\textsf Q}_p(\cdot)$ replaced by ${\mathtt t}_1^{-id} {\textsf q}_{p,i} (\cdot)$,
$0\le i\le 2$, are negligible, in the sense that they can be estimated
by the entropy and a small constant. It is enough to consider the term
${\textsf q}_{p,0}$.  Lemma \ref{s45} with $r_1 = {\mathtt t}_1{\mathtt t}_2$,
${\mathfrak a}({\mathtt j}) = {\mathtt t}_1^d \, \sum_{{\mathtt k}\in\Lambda_{{\mathtt j}}} [\,
J_{{\mathtt k}} - J_{2, {\mathtt j}}\,] \, H^{(1)}_{{\mathtt j}, {\mathtt k}}$ provides a
bound for the second term in \eqref{102b} (with ${\textsf Q}_p(\cdot)$
replaced by ${\textsf q}_{p,0} (\cdot)$) similar to \eqref{100}. Indeed, by
definition of $H^{(1)}_{{\mathtt j}, {\mathtt k}}$,
$|{\mathfrak a} ({\mathtt j})| \le {\mathfrak a}_{3,1}\, \Vert J\Vert_{C^1}\, ({\mathtt t}_1{\mathtt t}_2)^{d+2}/n^2$. By hypothesis,
$({\mathtt t}_1{\mathtt t}_2)^{d+2}/n^2 \le  ({\mathtt t}_1{\mathtt t}_2)^{d/2}$. Let
$F({\textsf m}) = {\textsf q}'_{p,0}({\textsf m}) \, \chi ({\textsf m})$.  By Lemma
\ref{s45}, there exists a finite constant ${\mathfrak a}_{3,1}$ such that
\begin{equation}
\label{103b}
\begin{aligned}
& \int \Big|\, \sum_{{\mathtt j}\in \Sigma^+_{{\mathtt t}_3}}
\big[ \, F({\textsf m}_{2,{\mathtt j}}) - E_{\nu^n_{\rho (\cdot)}} [F({\textsf m}_{2, {\mathtt j}})
] \, \big]
\, {\mathtt t}_1^d\,
\sum_{{\mathtt k}\in\Lambda_{{\mathtt j}}}  [\, J_{{\mathtt k}} - J_{2, {\mathtt j}}\,] \,
H^{(1)}_{{\mathtt j}, {\mathtt k}}\,\Big|
\, f\; d\nu^n_{\rho (\cdot)}
\\
&\quad \,\le \,
{\mathfrak a}_{3,1}\, \Vert J\Vert_{C^1} \,
\Big\{ \, H_n(f \,|\, \nu^n_{\rho (\cdot)}  )  \,+\,
\Big( \frac{{\mathtt t}_1{\mathtt t}_2}{n}\Big)^2\, 
\Big( \frac{n}{ ({\mathtt t}_1{\mathtt t}_2)^{1/2}} \Big)^d\, \Big\}\,.
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
The third term in \eqref{102b} (with ${\textsf Q}_p(\cdot)$ replaced by
${\textsf q}_{p,0} (\cdot)$) satisfies the same bound under the same
constraints.

We turn to the first term in \eqref{102b}.  Lemma \ref{s32} with
$r_1 = {\mathtt t}_1{\mathtt t}_2$,
${\mathfrak a} ({\mathtt j}) = ({\mathtt t}_2/{\mathtt t}_1)^d\, J_{2, {\mathtt j}}$ and
$F(x) = {\textsf q}_{p,2} (x)$ provides a bound for the first term in
\eqref{102b} (with ${\textsf Q}_p(\cdot)$ replaced by
${\mathtt t}_1^{-2d} {\textsf q}_{p,2} (\cdot)$) similar to \eqref{100}.  Since, by
hypothesis, ${\mathtt t}_2 \le K_2\, {\mathtt t}_1$, on the right-hand side of the
inequality, instead of the expression which appears in \eqref{100}, we
have
\begin{equation}
\label{104}
\Vert J\Vert_\infty \,
\Big\{   \, H_n(f \,|\, \nu^n_{\rho (\cdot)}  )  \,+\, \ln(2) \,+\,
C(p)\, e^{C(p) K_2^d}\, \Big( \frac{{\mathtt t}_2}{{\mathtt t}_1}\Big)^{2d}\, 
\Big( \frac{n}{ ({\mathtt t}_1{\mathtt t}_2)^{2}} \Big)^d\, \Big\}\,.
\end{equation}
As ${\mathtt t}_2\le K_2 \, {\mathtt t}_1$ and $K_2\ge 1$,
$C(p)\, \exp \{ C(p) K_2^d\}\, ({\mathtt t}_2/{\mathtt t}_1)^{2d} \le C(p)\,
K^{2d}_2 \exp \{ C(p) K_2^d\}$. This expression is less than or equal
to $\exp \{ C(p) K_2^d\}$ for some new constant $C(p)$.

In conclusion, all terms in \eqref{102b} can be estimated with the
exception of
\begin{equation*}
{\mathtt t}_2^d\, J_{2,{\mathtt j}}\, \Big\{\, {\textsf q}_{p,0}({\textsf m}_{2,{\mathtt j}}) +
\frac{1}{{\mathtt t}_1^{d} } \, {\textsf q}_{p,1}({\textsf m}_{2,{\mathtt j}})\, \Big\}
\,=\,
{\mathtt t}_2^d\, J_{2,{\mathtt j}}\, \Big\{\, {\textsf m}_{2,{\mathtt j}}^{p} \,+\,
\frac{1}{{\mathtt t}_1^{d} } \, \frac{p(p-1)}{2}\,
{\textsf m}_{2,{\mathtt j}}^{p-2}\, \chi({\textsf m}_{2,{\mathtt j}}) \Big\}
\,=\, {\mathtt t}_2^d\, J_{2,{\mathtt j}}\,   {\mathtt V}_{p} ({\textsf m}_{2,{\mathtt j}}) \,,
\end{equation*}
where the last identity follows from the definition \eqref{111} of
$W_{{\mathfrak p}}$ and ${\mathtt V}_p$.  To complete the proof of the proposition,
it remains to recollect all previous estimates.
<!-- end proof-23 -->
<!-- proof-24: body_md -->
The assertion follows from the bound \eqref{67}, and Propositions
\ref{s37}, \ref{s44}.  We may remove from the right-hand side of the
inequality obtained many terms which are less than or equal to other
terms. Here is a list.  The term
$(n/{\mathtt t}_1 {\mathtt t}_2)^d\, \exp \{- c_1 ({\mathtt t}_1 {\mathtt t}_2)^d\}$ is
dominated by the term $(n/[{\mathtt t}_1 {\mathtt t}_2]^2)^d$.  As
${\mathtt t}_2 \le K_2 {\mathtt t}_1$, ${\mathtt t}_1^{-2d}$ is dominated by
$({\mathtt t}_1{\mathtt t}_2)^{-d}$. As ${\mathtt t}_1{\mathtt t}_2 \le n$,
$({\mathtt t}_1{\mathtt t}_2/n)^6$ is dominated by $({\mathtt t}_1{\mathtt t}_2/n)^4$. Finally, the term $({\mathtt t}_1{\mathtt t}_2)^{-2d}$ is clearly
dominated by ${\mathtt t}_1^{-2d} {\mathtt t}_2^{-d}$.  This completes the proof
of the theorem.
<!-- end proof-24 -->
<!-- proposition-5: body_md -->
\label{s88}
Assume that the initial condition $u_0$ satisfies \eqref{255a}, and
belongs to $H^{3+\beta}$ for some $0<\beta<1$.  Let $u(t,x)$ be the
solution of the hydrodynamic equation \eqref{127}.  Fix $\delta_0>0$,
a cylinder function $h\colon \{0,1\}^{{\mathbb Z}^d} \to {\mathbb R}$, and a
function $G$ in $C^{0,2}({\mathbb R}_+ \times {\mathbb T}^d)$. In dimension $1$ we
also fix $0<b<1/6$, and in dimension $3$ a constant $\kappa>1$ and
$0< {\mathtt e} < 1/30$.  Then, there exist a finite positive constant
${\mathfrak c}_{1,3} = {\mathfrak c}_{1,3} (h, \delta_0)$ (in dimension $1$,
${\mathfrak c}_{1,3}$ also depends on $b$), and an integer
$n_0= n_0(\delta_0, {\mathfrak r}, h, \Vert u\Vert_{T,3}, \Vert G\Vert_{T,2})$
(in dimension $3$, $n_0$ also depends on $\kappa$) such that
\begin{align*}
& \Big|\, {\mathbb E}_{\mu_n} \Big[\, \int_0^t
\sum_{x\in {\mathbb T}^d_n} G (s, x/n)\,
\Pi_{u(s, \cdot), h}(x, \eta^n(s)) \, ds \,  \Big] \,\Big|
\\
& \;\le \;
\int_0^t   \delta_0\, n^2\, I_n  (f_s;  \nu^n_{u(s, \cdot) } ) \; ds
\,+\, {\mathfrak c}_{1,3} \int_0^t  
\,\big\{   \, {\mathtt K}_{d,1} (s) \, H_n (f_s\,|\, \nu^n_{u(s, \cdot)})
\,+\, {\mathtt K}_{d,2} (s)  \,\big\}\, ds
\end{align*}
for all $ 0\le t\le T$, and $n\ge n_0$. In this formula,
\begin{gather*}
{\color{blue} {\mathtt K}_{1,1}(s) } \, :=\, \Vert G(s) \Vert_{\infty} (1 + \Vert G(s)
\Vert_{\infty}) + \Vert G(s) \Vert_{C^2}\,, \quad
{\color{blue} {\mathtt K}_{1,2}(s) }  \,:= \, {\mathtt K}_{1,1}(s) \, n^{(1/3)+b}\,,
\\
{\color{blue} {\mathtt K}_{2,1} (s) } \,:=\, \exp\{ {\mathfrak c}_{1,3}\, \Vert G(s)\Vert_{C^1}\}
+ \Vert G(s) \Vert_{C^2}\,, \quad
{\color{blue} {\mathtt K}_{2,2} (s)} \,:=\, {\mathtt K}_{2,1} (s) \, n^{4/5}\,,
\\
{\color{blue} {\mathtt K}_{3,1} (s) } \,:=\, \Vert G(s) \Vert_{C^2}\,, \quad
{\color{blue} {\mathtt K}_{3,2} (s) } \,:=\, {\mathtt K}_{3,3} (s)\, n^{3/2 - 2{\mathtt e}}
\,+\, \Vert G(s) \, \Vert_\infty\,  
\frac{n^{3/2}}{\kappa^3}  \,,
\\
{\color{blue} {\mathtt K}_{3,3} (s)} \, := 
\Vert G(s) \Vert_{C^2} \, \kappa^4 \,+\,
\kappa^{1/2}\, e^{{\mathfrak c}_{1,3} \,\kappa^6\,[1 + \Vert G(s)\Vert_{C^1}]}
\end{gather*}
<!-- end proposition-5 -->
<!-- remark-23: body_md -->
It is enough to prove this proposition without the absolute value
and observe that the same argument applies to $-\, G$ in place of $G$.
<!-- end remark-23 -->
<!-- proof-25: body_md -->
We start with $d=1$, $2$.  Fix $T>0$, $0<b<1/6$. By \eqref{118},
the bound \eqref{108} for $I_n(s)$, the one for
${\mathfrak R}^{(4)}_{t,n}$ stated in Lemma \ref{s41}, and Proposition
\ref{s88} with $\delta_0 = 1/(3d)$,
\begin{equation*}
H_n(f_t | \nu^n_{u( t,\cdot)} ) \; \leq\;
H_n(f_0 | \nu^n_{u_0(\cdot)} )
\, - \,  \int_0^t  n^2\, I_n(f_s ; \nu^n_{u( s,\cdot)})\, ds
\, +\, {\mathfrak c}_{1,4} \, \int_0^t   \big\{\, H_n(f_s | \nu^n_{u( s,\cdot)} )
\,+\, n^{a_d}  \big\} \; ds  
\end{equation*}
for all $n$ sufficiently large and $0\le t\le T$. In this formula,
$a_1= (1/3) + b$ in dimension $1$ and $a_2=4/5$ in dimension $2$.  As
$b<1/6$, apply Gronwall's inequality to complete the proof for $n$
large. For $n$ small the bound follows from equation \eqref{118},
elementary bounds for the terms on the right-hand side of this
inequality, and adjusting the constant ${\mathfrak c}_{1,4}$.

The proof in dimension $3$ is similar.  Fix $T>0$, $\kappa>1$. Let
$0<{\mathtt e}<1/30$.  By \eqref{118}, the bound \eqref{108} for $I_n(s)$,
the one for ${\mathfrak R}^{(4)}_{t,n}$ stated in Lemma \ref{s41}, and
Proposition \ref{s88} with $\delta_0 = 1/(3d)$,
\begin{align*}
H_n(f_t | \nu^n_{u( t,\cdot)} ) \; &\leq\;
H_n(f_0 | \nu^n_{u_0(\cdot)} )
\, - \,  \int_0^t  n^2\, I_n(f_s ; \nu^n_{u( s,\cdot)})\, ds
\\
& +\, {\mathfrak c}_{1,4}   \, \int_0^t   \Big\{\, \, H_n(f_s | \nu^n_{u( s,\cdot)} )
\,+\, e^{{\mathfrak c}_{1,3} \kappa^6} \, n^{3/2-2{\mathtt e}} \,+\,
\frac{n^{3/2}}{\kappa^3} \Big\} \; ds  
\end{align*}
for all $n\ge n_1 = n_1(\kappa, {\mathfrak r}, \Vert u \Vert_{T,3}, h)$.  For
$n \ge n_2(\kappa, {\mathfrak r}, \Vert u \Vert_{T,3}, h)$,
$e^{{\mathfrak c}_{1,3} \kappa^6} \, n^{3/2-2{\mathtt e}} \le n^{3/2} / \kappa^3$.
Therefore, by Gronwall's inequality, 
\begin{equation*}
H_n (f_t \,|\, \nu^n_{u(t, \cdot)}  ) \,\le\,
\Big\{\, H_n (f_0 \,|\, \nu^n_{u_0 (\cdot)}  ) \,+\,
{\mathfrak c}_{1,4}  
\frac{n^{3/2}}{\kappa^3} \,\Big\}\, e^{{\mathfrak c}_{1,4} \,  t}
\end{equation*}
for all $n\ge n_0 = n_1 \vee n_2$, $0\le t\le T$.
<!-- end proof-25 -->
<!-- lemma-16: body_md -->
\label{s51}
Fix a function $J\colon {\mathbb T}^d \to {\mathbb R}$ of class
$C^2({\mathbb T}^d)$. Then, there exists a finite constant $C_1$ such that
\begin{gather*}
\int \big| \, W^{(\ref{s51})} _n \, \big| \, 
f\, d\nu^n_{u( t, \cdot)} \,\le\,
{\mathtt R}^{(\ref{s51})} _n
\\
\text{where}\;\;
{\color{blue} {\mathtt R}^{(\ref{s51})} _n}\,:=\,
 \Vert J\Vert_{C^2} \,
\Big\{\, H_n(f \,|\, \nu^n_{u(t, \cdot)}  )  \,+\, \ln(2) \,+\,
C_1\, \Big( \frac{r_1}{n}\Big)^4  \, n^d\,\Big\}
\end{gather*}
for all densities $f$ with respect to $\nu^n_{u( t, \cdot)}$, and
$0\le t\le T$.
<!-- end lemma-16 -->
<!-- proof-26: body_md -->
Fix $0\le t\le T$, a function $J\colon {\mathbb T}^d \to {\mathbb R}$ of class
$C^2({\mathbb T}^d)$, and a density $f$ with respect to
$\nu^n_{u( t, \cdot)}$. Recall the definition of the cube $\Sigma_b$
introduced in \eqref{190}, and let 
\begin{align*}
J^{(1)} (x/n)\,=\, \frac{1}{|\Sigma_{b_1}|}\,
\sum_{y\in \Sigma_{b_1}} J \Big( \frac{y+x}{n}\Big) \,, \quad
J^{(2)} (x/n)\,=\, \frac{1}{|\Sigma_{b_1}|}\,
\sum_{y\in \Sigma_{b_1}} J^{(1)} \Big( \frac{y+x}{n}\Big) \,.
\end{align*}
Note that we use here the centered cube $\Sigma_{b_1}$ instead of
$\Sigma^+_{b_1}$. The reason is that we wish the first order term in
the Taylor expansion
$\sum_{y\in \Sigma_{b_1}} [\, J((x+y)/n) - J(x/n)\,]$ to vanish.  As
$J$ is of class $C^2({\mathbb T}^d)$, the absolute value of the difference
$J(x/n)\, -\, J^{(1)}(x/n) $ is bounded by
$C_1\, \Vert J\Vert_{C^2}\, (r_1/n)^2$ uniformly in $x$.  Similarly,
adding and subtracting $J^{(1)}(x/n)$, $J(x/n)\, -\, J^{(2)}(x/n) $ is
also bounded by $C_1 \, \Vert J\Vert_{C^2} \, (r_1/n)^2$. Therefore, by
Lemma \ref{s47} with $h(\eta) = \eta_0$, $\gamma = 1/\Vert J\Vert_{C^2}$
\begin{align*}
& \int \Big| \, \sum_{x\in {\mathbb T}^d_n} 
\big\{\, J(x/n)\, -\,  J^{(2)}(x/n) \, \big\}
\big[\, \eta(x) - u( t, x/n) \,\big] \,\Big | \, 
f\, d\nu^n_{u( t, \cdot)}
\\
&\quad
\,\le \,  \Vert J\Vert_{C^2} \,
\Big\{\, H_n(f \,|\, \nu^n_{u (t, \cdot)}  )  \,+\, \ln(2)  \,+\,
C_1\, \Big( \frac{r_1}{n}\Big)^4  \, n^d\,\Big\} \,.
\end{align*}
Changing variables, and by symmetry, 
\begin{align*}
& \sum_{x\in {\mathbb T}^d_n}  J^{(2)}(x/n) \, 
\big[\, \eta(x) - u( t, x/n) \,\big]
\, =\, \sum_{x\in {\mathbb T}^d_n}  J^{(1)}(x/n) \,
\frac{1}{|\Sigma_{b_1}|}\,
\sum_{y\in \Sigma_{b_1}} 
\big[\, \eta(x+y) - u( t, [x+y]/n) \,\big]
\\
&\quad =\, 
\sum_{x\in {\mathbb T}^d_n} \,
\frac{1}{|\Sigma_{b_1}|}\,
\sum_{z\in \Sigma_{b_1}} J \Big( \frac{z+x}{n}\Big)
\frac{1}{|\Sigma_{b_1}|}\,
\sum_{y\in \Sigma_{b_1}} 
\big[\, \eta(x+y) - u( t, [x+y]/n) \,\big]\,.
\end{align*}
As $r_1 = 2b_1+1$, $|\Sigma_{b_1}| = |\Sigma^+_{r_1}|$ and
$x+\Sigma_{b_1} = x - {\mathbf b}_1 + \Sigma^+_{r_1} $, where
${\mathbf b}_1 = (b_1, \dots, b_1)$. Thus the previous expression can be
rewritten as
\begin{align*}
\sum_{y\in B_{{\mathtt 0}}} \sum_{{\mathtt k} \in \Sigma^+_{r_2}}
J(y+ B_{{\mathtt k}} ) \,
\big[\, {\textsf m}_{y, {\mathtt k}}  - u(t, y+ B_{{\mathtt k}}) \,\big]\,,
\end{align*}
which completes the proof of the lemma.
<!-- end proof-26 -->
<!-- corollary-7: body_md -->
\label{s52}
Fix two functions $F$, $G\colon {\mathbb T}^d \to {\mathbb R}$ of class
$C^2({\mathbb T}^d)$. Then, there exists a finite constant $C_1$ such that
\begin{gather*}
\int \big | \, W^{(\ref{s52})}_n \, \big|
\, f\, d\nu^n_{u( t, \cdot)} \,\le \, {\mathtt R}^{(\ref{s52})}_n\,,
\\
\text{where}\;\;
{\color{blue} {\mathtt R}^{(\ref{s52})}_n}\,:=\,
C_1\, \Vert F\Vert_{C^2}\, \Vert G\Vert_{C^2} \,\Big\{
H_n(f \,|\, \nu^n_{u (t, \cdot)}  )  \,+\, \ln(2) \,+\,
\Big( \frac{r_1}{n}\Big)^4  \, n^d\,\Big\}\,,
\end{gather*}
for all densities $f$ with respect to $\nu^n_{u( t, \cdot)}$, and
$0\le t\le T$.
<!-- end corollary-7 -->
<!-- proof-27: body_md -->
Fix two functions $F$, $G$ in $C^2({\mathbb T}^d)$.  Let
\begin{align*}
H(y+B_{{\mathtt k}}) \, &=\, \frac{1}{| B_{{\mathtt k}}|} \,  \sum_{x\in y+B_{{\mathtt k}}}
\big\{\, F(x/n) - F(y+ B_{{\mathtt k}})\big\}\,
\big\{\, G(x/n) - G(y+B_{{\mathtt k}})\big\}
\\
&=\, \frac{1}{| B_{{\mathtt k}}|} \,  \sum_{x\in y+B_{{\mathtt k}}}
F(x/n) \, G(x/n) \,-\, F(y+B_{{\mathtt k}}) \, G(y+B_{{\mathtt k}}) \,.
\end{align*}
As $F$, $G$ are Lipschitz-continuous,
$|H( y + B_{{\mathtt k}})|\le \Vert F\Vert_{C^1}\, \Vert G\Vert_{C^1}\,
(r_1/n)^2$. Thus, summing by parts to recover $\eta_x - u(t,x/n)$ from
${\textsf m}_{y+ B_{{\mathtt k}}} - u(t, y+ B_{{\mathtt k}})$, by Lemma \ref{s47}
with $h=\eta_0$, $\gamma =1/(\Vert F\Vert_{C^1}\, \Vert G\Vert_{C^1})$,
\begin{align*}
& \int \Big| \, \sum_{y\in B_{{\mathtt 0}}} \sum_{{\mathtt k} \in \Sigma^+_{r_2}}
H(y+ B_{{\mathtt k}} ) \,
\big[\, {\textsf m}_{y+ B_{{\mathtt k}}}
- u(t, y+ B_{{\mathtt k}}) \,\big] \, \Big | \, 
f\, d\nu^n_{u( t, \cdot)}
\\
& \quad \,\le \,
\Vert F\Vert_{C^1}\, \Vert G\Vert_{C^1} \,\Big\{
H_n(f \,|\, \nu^n_{u(t, \cdot)}  )  \,+\, \ln(2) \,+\,
C_1\, \Big( \frac{r_1}{n}\Big)^4  \, n^d\,\Big\}
\end{align*}
for all densities $f$ with respect to $\nu^n_{u(t, \cdot)} $.  The
assertion of the corollary follows from Lemma \ref{s51} with $J = FG$
and this bound.
<!-- end proof-27 -->
<!-- proof-28: body_md -->
Fix $0<b<1/6$, $\delta_0>0$, and $0\le s\le t \le T$. Recall equation
\eqref{115} to rewrite the sum appearing on the left-hand side of the
statement of the proposition as
\begin{align}
\label{180}
\frac{1}{|B_{{\mathtt 0}} |}\, 
\sum_{y \in B_{{\mathtt 0}}}  \sum_{{\mathtt k}\in \Sigma^+_{\ell_2}}
\sum_{x\in y+ B^o_{{\mathtt k}}} 
\frac{|B_{{\mathtt 0}} |}{|B^o_{{\mathtt 0}} |}\, 
G(s,x/n)\,  \Pi_{u(s, \cdot) , h} (x, \eta)\,.
\end{align}
We consider below the case $y=0$ and make sure at each step that the
estimate is uniform over $y \in B_{{\mathtt 0}}$.  The proof in dimension
$1$ does not require a multi-scale analysis and relies solely on
Corollary \ref{s46} and the estimates presented in the current
section. Recall the notation introduced in that corollary, in
particular the constant ${\mathfrak a}'_2 = {\mathfrak a}'_2({\mathfrak c}_{\rm SG})$ which will
appear below.

Set $\ell_1 = n^a$, where $a=(2/3) - b$.  There exists a constant
$C_0 = C_0(h)$ such that the ratio $|B_{{\mathtt 0}} |/|B^o_{{\mathtt 0}} |$ is
bounded by $C_0$. As $b>0$, there exists ${\color{blue} n_0} : = n_0(h,G, \delta)$
such that
$\Vert h\Vert_\infty\, \Vert G(s)\Vert_\infty\, \ell^{d+2}_1 \le {\mathfrak a}'_2 \,\delta\, n^2$ for all $n\ge n_0$, $0\le s\le T$.  Thus, by
Corollary \ref{s46} with $\rho(\cdot) = u(s, \cdot)$,
$\delta = \delta_0/C_0$, and $L_2 = \ell_2$, and by \eqref{120} with
$r_1=\ell_1$,
\begin{equation*}
\begin{aligned}
& \frac{|B_{{\mathtt 0}} |}{|B^o_{{\mathtt 0}} |} \sum_{{\mathtt k}\in
\Sigma^+_{\ell_2}} \int \sum_{x\in B^o_{{\mathtt k}}} G(s,x/n)\,
\Big(\, \tau_x h \, - \, E_{\nu^n_{u( s,\cdot)} } \big[\, \tau_x h
\,\big] \,-\,  \big[\, {\mathtt p}_h ({\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}}) \,-\, {\mathtt p}_h ( u(s, {\mathtt k})) \,\big] \,
\Big)\, f_s \, d\nu^n_{u(s,\cdot)}
\\
& \quad \,\le\, \delta_0\, n^2\, I_n(f_s ; \nu^n_{u( s,\cdot)} )
\,+\, {\mathfrak c}_{1,3} \, {\mathtt K}_{1}(G_s)\,
\Big\{ \,  H_n (f_s \,|\, \nu^n_{u( s,\cdot)} ) \,+\,
n^{2a-1} \,+\, n^{1-2a} \,+\, n^{1-a} \,\Big\}
\end{aligned}
\end{equation*}
for all $n\ge n_0$. In this formula,
${\color{blue} {\mathtt K}_{1}(G_s) } = \Vert G(s) \Vert_{\infty} ( 1+ \Vert G(s)
\Vert_{\infty}) + \Vert G(s) \Vert_{C^1}$.  As $a>0$,
$n^{1-2a} \le n^{1-a}$ and $1\le n^{2a-1} + n^{1-a} $. The constant
$\delta = \delta_0/C_0$ multiplying $I_n(f_s ; \nu^n_{u( s,\cdot)} )$
becomes $\delta_0$ because we overestimate the ratio
$|B_{{\mathtt 0}} |/|B^o_{{\mathtt 0}} |$ by $C_0$.

On the other hand, the inequality \eqref{135}, with $r_1=\ell_1$,
$F(\cdot) = G(s, \cdot)$, $H(\cdot) = {\mathtt p}_h'(\cdot)$, takes care of
the linear term in $\Pi_{u(s, \cdot) , h} (x, \eta)$ at an extra cost
$n^{4a-3}$. This estimate and the previous one yield that
\begin{equation*}
\begin{aligned}
& \int
\frac{|B_{{\mathtt 0}} |}{|B^o_{{\mathtt 0}} |}\,
\sum_{{\mathtt k}\in \Sigma^+_{\ell_2}}
\sum_{x\in B^o_{{\mathtt k}}} 
G(s,x/n)\,  \Pi_{u(s, \cdot) , h} (x, \eta)\, 
f_s \, d\nu^n_{u( s, \cdot)}
\\
& \quad \le
\int \sum_{{\mathtt k}\in \Sigma^+_{\ell_2}}  
\ell_1^d\,  G (s, {\mathtt k}) \, \Big\{ \, {\mathtt p}_h({\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}})
\,-\, {\mathtt p}_h( u(s, {\mathtt k})) \, -\,
{\mathtt p}_h' ( u(s,{\mathtt k}) ) 
\, [\,{\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}}  - u(s,{\mathtt k})\,]\,
\Big\}\,
f_s \, d\nu^n_{u(s,\cdot)}
\\
& \quad
\,+\, \delta_0 \, n^2\, I_n(f_s ; \nu^n_{u( s,\cdot)}  )
\,+\, {\mathfrak c}_{1,3} \, {\mathtt K}_{1,1}(G_s)   \,
\Big\{   \, H_n (f_s\,|\, \nu^n_{u( s,\cdot)}  )
\,+\, n^{2a-1} \,+\, n^{1-a} \,\Big\} \,.
\end{aligned}
\end{equation*}
We used here that $4a -3 < 1-a$ because $a\le 2/3$.  By Taylor's
development, the expression inside braces in the first line is bounded
by $C_0 (h) [\,{\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}} - u(s,{\mathtt k})\,]^2$. By Lemma \ref{l02}
with $r_1=\ell_1$, the first line is therefore bounded by
$C_1 \, \Vert G(s) \Vert_\infty \, \{ \, H_n (f_s\,|\, \nu^n_{u(
s,\cdot)} ) + n^{1-a}\}$. To complete the proof of the proposition for
$n$ large, it remains to recollect all previous estimates.
<!-- end proof-28 -->
<!-- proof-29: body_md -->
Fix $\delta_0>0$, $0\le s\le t \le T$. As in dimension $1$, we
estimate the expectation of \eqref{180} for $y=0$ with respect to
$f_s \, d\nu^n_{u(s, \cdot)}$.  The argument is based on Corollaries
\ref{s46}, \ref{s48} and the estimates presented in this section.

Set $\ell_1 = n^{2/5}$.  In dimension $2$, Corollary \ref{s46}
requires $\ell_1$ to be bounded by $c_1 n^{1/2}$ for some constant
$c_1$. This condition is thus satisfied. As in the proof in one
dimension, by Corollary \ref{s46} with $\delta=\delta_0/[2 C_0(h)]$, and
the previous choice of $\ell_1$, setting $n = \ell_1\, L_2$,
\begin{align*}
& \frac{|B_{{\mathtt 0}} |}{|B^o_{{\mathtt 0}} |}  \sum_{{\mathtt k}\in \Sigma^+_{L_2}}  \int
\sum_{x\in B^o_{{\mathtt k}}} G(s,x/n)\,
\Big\{   \, 
\tau_x h \, -
\, E_{\nu^n_{u( s,\cdot)} } \big[\, \tau_x h \,\big]
\,-\,   \big\{ \, {\mathtt p}_h({\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}})
\,-\, E_{\nu^n_{u( s,\cdot)} } \big[\,
{\mathtt p}_h({\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}}) \,\big] \,\big\} \, \Big\} \,
f_s\, d\nu^n_{u(s,\cdot)}
\nonumber
\\
& \quad
\,\le\, \frac{\delta_0}{2} \, n^2\, I_n(f_s ; \nu^n_{u( s,\cdot)}  )
\,+\, {\mathfrak c}_{1,3} \, {\mathtt K}_1 (G_s) \,
\Big\{   \, H_n (f_s \,|\, \nu^n_{u( s,\cdot)}  )
\,+\, n^{4/5} \,\Big\} 
\end{align*}
for all $n\ge n_0(h, G, \delta)$. The constant ${\mathtt K}_1 (G_s) $ is
introduced in the previous subsection.

Since in dimension $d=2$ in Corollary \ref{s46} we are forced to take
cubes of side length $\ell_1 \ll \sqrt{n}$, the last step in the proof of
Proposition \ref{s88}, which consists in applying Lemma \ref{l02} (see
the proof in dimension $1$), does not provide a good bound for cubes
of this size. We are thus led to appeal to the multi-scale analysis to
increase the size of the cube. This is the role of Corollary
\ref{s48}.

Set $\ell_2 = n^{1/5}$, $\ell_3 = n^{2/5}$ so that
$\ell_1\ell_2\ell_3 = n$.  With these choices, the hypotheses of
Corollary \ref{s48} are satisfied for $K_1=1$ and $\epsilon <1$. Thus
by this result with $\delta =\delta_0/2$,
\begin{align*}
& \int
\sum_{{\mathtt j} \in \Sigma^+_{\ell_3}}
\sum_{{\mathtt k} \in \Lambda_{{\mathtt j}}}  \ell_1^d\, G(s, B_{\mathtt k}) \, \Big\{\,
{\mathtt p}_h({\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}})
\,-\, E_{\nu^n_{u( s,\cdot)} } \big[\,
{\mathtt p}_h({\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}}) \,\big]
\,-\, 
\big(\, {\mathtt p}_h ({\textsf m}_{2, {\mathtt j}})
- E_{\nu^n_{u( s,\cdot)} } [\, {\mathtt p}_h ({\textsf m}_{2, {\mathtt j}}) \, ] \,\big)
\, \Big\}\,
f_s \, d\nu^n_{u( s,\cdot)}
\nonumber
\\
&  \le\, \frac{\delta_0}{2} \, n^2 \,  I_n  ( f_s \,;\, \nu^n_{u (s, \cdot)} )
\,+\, {\mathfrak c}_{1,3} \, {\mathtt K}_2(G(s))
\,\Big\{   \, H_n (f_s \,|\, \nu^n_{u(s, \cdot)}) \,+\,
n^{4/5} \,\Big\}
\end{align*}
for all $n\ge n_1$, where ${\color{blue} n_1} = n_1({\mathfrak c}_{1,3}, h,
\delta_0)$. In this formula,
${\color{blue} {\mathtt K}_2(G(s))} := [1+\Vert G(s)\Vert_{C^1}]^2 \, \exp\{{\mathfrak c}_{1,3} [ 1+\Vert G(s)\Vert_{C^1}]\,\}$.

The two previous bounds together with \eqref{120} with
$r_1=\ell_1\ell_2 = n^{3/5}$ [replacing
$E_{\nu^n_{u( s,\cdot)} } [\, {\mathtt p}_h ({\textsf m}_{2, {\mathtt j}}) \, ]$ by
${\mathtt p}_h(u(s, B_{2,{\mathtt j}}))$] yield that
\begin{align*}
& \frac{|B_{{\mathtt 0}} |}{|B^o_{{\mathtt 0}} |}
\sum_{{\mathtt j} \in \Sigma^+_{\ell_3}}
\sum_{{\mathtt k} \in \Lambda_{{\mathtt j}}}   \int
\sum_{x\in B^o_{{\mathtt k}}} G(s,x/n)\,
\Big\{   \, 
\tau_x h \, -
\, E_{\nu^n_{u( s,\cdot)} } \big[\, \tau_x h \,\big]
\,-\,   \big\{ \, {\mathtt p}_h({\textsf m}_{2,{\mathtt j}})
\,-\, 
{\mathtt p}_h(u(s,  B_{2,{\mathtt j}}))  \,\big\} \, \Big\} \,
f_s\, d\nu^n_{u(s,\cdot)}
\nonumber
\\
& \quad
\,\le\, \delta_0 \, n^2\, I_n(f_s ; \nu^n_{u( s,\cdot)}  )
\,+\, {\mathfrak c}_{1,3} \, {\mathtt K}_2(G(s))\, \Big\{   \, H_n (f_s\,|\, \nu^n_{u( s,\cdot)}  )
\,+\, n^{4/5} \,\Big\} 
\end{align*}
for all $n$ sufficiently large.

The inequality \eqref{135}, with $r_1=\ell_1\ell_2$,
$F(\cdot) = G(s, \cdot)$, $H(\cdot) = {\mathtt p}_h'(\cdot)$, takes care of
the linear term in $\Pi_{u(s, \cdot) , h} (x, \eta)$ at an extra cost
$n^{2/5}$. This estimate and the previous one yield that
\begin{equation*}
\begin{aligned}
& \int
\frac{|B_{{\mathtt 0}} |}{|B^o_{{\mathtt 0}} |}\,
\sum_{{\mathtt k}\in \Sigma^+_{L_2}}
\sum_{x\in B^o_{{\mathtt k}}} 
G(s,x/n)\,  \Pi_{u(s, \cdot) , h} (x, \eta)\, 
f_s \, d\nu^n_{u( s, \cdot)}
\\
& \quad \le
\int \sum_{{\mathtt j}\in \Sigma^+_{\ell_3}}  
(\ell_1\ell_2)^d\,  G (s, B_{2,{\mathtt j}}) \, \Big\{ \, {\mathtt p}_h({\textsf m}_{2,{\mathtt j}})
\,-\, {\mathtt p}_h( u(s, B_{2,{\mathtt j}})) \, -\,
{\mathtt p}_h' ( u(s, B_{2,{\mathtt j}}) ) 
\, [\,{\textsf m}_{2, {\mathtt j}}  - u(s,B_{2,{\mathtt j}} )\,]\,
\Big\}\,
f_s \, d\nu^n_{u(s,\cdot)}
\\
& \quad
\,+\, \delta_0 \, n^2\, I_n(f_s ; \nu^n_{u( s,\cdot)}  )
\,+\, {\mathfrak c}_{1,3} \, {\mathtt K}_3(G(s)) \, \Big\{   \, H_n (f_s\,|\, \nu^n_{u( s,\cdot)}  )
\,+\, n^{4/5} \,\Big\} \,,
\end{aligned}
\end{equation*}
where ${\color{blue}  {\mathtt K}_3(G(s)) } := \, {\mathtt K}_2(G(s)) + \Vert G(s)\Vert_{C^2}$.
By Lemma \ref{l02} with $r_1=\ell_1\ell_2$, this expression is less
than or equal to
\begin{align*}
\delta_0  \, n^2 \,  I_n  ( f_s \,;\, \nu^n_{u (s, \cdot)} )
\,+\, {\mathfrak c}_{1,3} \,{\mathtt K}_3(G(s)) \,
\Big\{   \, H_n (f_s\,|\, \nu^n_{u(s, \cdot)}) \,+\, n^{4/5} \,\Big\}\,.
\end{align*}
This completes the proof in dimension $2$.
<!-- end proof-29 -->
<!-- lemma-17: body_md -->
\label{s49}
Fix a density profile $\rho\colon {\mathbb T}^d\to (0,1)$ satisfying the
hypotheses of Theorem \ref{s01}, a cylinder function $h$, a function
$J\colon {\mathbb T}^d \to {\mathbb R}$ of class $C^1$, and constants $\delta'>0$,
$0<{\mathtt e}<1/30$, and $\kappa \ge 1$. Let $\ell_1= n^{1/4-{\mathtt e}}$,
$\ell_2= n^{3/20- {\mathtt e}}$, $\ell_3= \kappa \, n^{1/10+2{\mathtt e}}$.
Then, there exist finite constants ${\mathfrak a}_{3,3} = {\mathfrak a}_{3,3} (h)$,
and an integer
$n_0=n_0(\kappa, \delta', {\mathfrak r}, \Vert \rho\Vert_{C^3}, h, \Vert
J\Vert_\infty)$ such that
\begin{align*}
& \sum_{x  \in {\mathbb T}^d_{n}}  \int
J(x/n)\, \big\{   \,  \tau_x h \, -
\, E_{\nu^n_{\rho(\cdot)} } \big[\, \tau_x h \,\big] \, \big\}\,
f\, d\nu^n_{\rho(\cdot)}
\\
& \quad 
\, \le\,
\frac{1}{|B_{{\mathtt 0}} |}\, 
\sum_{y \in B_{{\mathtt 0}}}  \sum_{{\mathtt i}\in \Sigma^+_{L_4}}  \int
(\ell_1\ell_2\ell_3)^d J(B_{3, {\mathtt i}, y} )\, \big\{   \, 
{\mathtt p}_h({\textsf m}_{3,{\mathtt i}, y})
\,-\, E_{\nu^n_{\rho(\cdot)} } \big[\,
{\mathtt p}_h({\textsf m}_{3,{\mathtt i}, y}) \,\big] \,\big\} \, 
f\, d\nu^n_{\rho(\cdot)}
\nonumber
\\
& \quad
\,+\, \delta' \, n^2\, I_n(f ; \nu^n_{\rho(\cdot)}  )
\,+\, {\mathfrak a}_{3,3}\, \Vert J\Vert_{C^1}\, H_n (f\,|\, \nu^n_{\rho(\cdot)}  )
\,+\,  \,\big[\, {\mathfrak a}_{3,3} (\delta', h) \,  \Vert J\Vert_{C^1}
\,+\, {\mathtt K}_4(\kappa, J) \,\big] \, n^{3/2 - 2{\mathtt e}}  
\end{align*}
for all densities $f$ with respect to $\nu^n_{\rho(\cdot)}$, and
$n\ge n_0$. In this formula, $B_{3, {\mathtt i}, y} = y + B_{3, {\mathtt i}}$,
and
${\color{blue} {\mathtt K}_4(\kappa, J) } = \kappa^{1/2}\, e^{({\mathfrak c}_{\rm
LS}/\delta') \,\kappa^6\, [1+{\mathfrak a}_{3,3}]\,[1 + \Vert J\Vert_{C^1}]}
$.
<!-- end lemma-17 -->
<!-- proof-30: body_md -->
Let ${\color{blue} L_2} := \ell_2\ell_3L_4$, and recall that $L_3 = \ell_3 L_4$.
Recall equation \eqref{180}. We restrict our attention to the term
$y=0$, and estimate the expression
\begin{align}
\label{181}
\frac{|B_{{\mathtt 0}} |}{|B^o_{{\mathtt 0}} |}\,
\int 
\sum_{{\mathtt k}\in \Sigma^+_{L_2}}
\sum_{x\in B^o_{{\mathtt k}}} 
J(x/n)\, \big\{   \,  \tau_x h \, -
\, E_{\nu^n_{\rho(\cdot)} } \big[\, \tau_x h \,\big] \, \big\}
\, f\, d\nu^n_{\rho(\cdot)} \, .
\end{align}

Fix $\delta'>0$ and $0<{\mathtt e}<1/30$. By Theorem \ref{s01} with
$\delta = \delta'/[8C_0(h)]$, $\ell_1 = n^{1/4 - {\mathtt e}}$, as ${\mathtt e}<1/30$, there
exists a finite constant ${\mathfrak a}_{3,3}$, and an integer
$n_0 = n_0(\delta', h, \Vert J\Vert_\infty)$ such that
\eqref{181} is bounded above by
\begin{align}
\label{121b}
& \sum_{{\mathtt k}\in \Sigma^+_{L_2}}  \int
\ell_1^d \, J(B_{{\mathtt k}})\, \big\{ \, {\mathtt p}_h({\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}})
\,-\, E_{\nu^n_{\rho(\cdot)} } \big[\,
{\mathtt p}_h ({\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}}) \,\big] \,\big\} \, 
f\, d\nu^n_{\rho(\cdot)}
\nonumber
\\
& \quad
\,+ \,  \sum_{{\mathtt k}\in \Sigma^+_{L_2}}  \int
J (B_{{\mathtt k}})  \, \Big\{ \, {\mathtt q}_h({\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}}) 
\,-\,  E_{\nu^n_{\rho(\cdot)}  } \big[\,
{\mathtt q}_h({\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}}) \,\big] 
\, \Big\}\,
f\, d\nu^n_{\rho(\cdot)}
\\
& \quad
\,+\, \frac{\delta'}{8} \, n^2\, I_n(f ; \nu^n_{\rho(\cdot)}  )
\,+\, {\mathfrak a}_{3,1}\, \Vert J\Vert_{\infty}
\, H_n (f\,|\, \nu^n_{\rho(\cdot)}  )
\,+\, {\mathfrak a}_{3,3}\, \Vert J\Vert_{C^1}\,
\frac{1}{\delta'}\, n^{3/2 - 2{\mathtt e}}  
\nonumber
\end{align}
for all $n\ge n_0$.  Note that the term ${\mathtt q}_h$, via $W^h_{{\mathtt k},x}$ came with a multiplicative constant $\ell_1^{-d}$ which canceled
the factor $\ell_1^d$ as the sum in ${\mathtt k}$ is performed over
$(n/\ell_1)^d$ terms only. 
As we are far from cubes of side length $n^{1/2}$, we apply Theorem
\ref{s26} to increase their size. We examine in detail the expression
${\mathtt p}_h({\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}}) \,-\, E_{\nu^n_{\rho(\cdot)} } [\, {\mathtt p}_h({\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}}) \,] $. The same arguments apply to
${\mathtt q}_h({\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}}) \,-\, E_{\nu^n_{\rho(\cdot)} } [\, {\mathtt q}_h({\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}}) \,] $, with a simplification due to the extra
implicit factor $\ell_1^{-d}$. Recall the definition of $W_{{\mathfrak p}, {\mathtt j}}$
introduced in \eqref{111}.

Fix $0<\epsilon<1$, and recall that $\ell_2 = n^{3/20 - {\mathtt e}}$. A direct
calculation shows that there exists an integer
$n_1 = n_1(\epsilon, \delta', {\mathfrak r}, \Vert \rho\Vert_{C^3}, h)$ such
that for all $n\ge n_1$, the conditions of Theorem \ref{s26} with
${\mathtt t}_1 = \ell_1$, ${\mathtt t}_2 =\ell_2$ are satisfied with
$K_1=K_2=1$.  Thus, applying Theorem \ref{s26} with these choices and
$\delta = \delta'/8$, we obtain a finite constant ${\mathfrak a}_{3,3}$ such
that
\begin{align}
\label{122b}
& \int
\sum_{{\mathtt j} \in \Sigma^+_{L_3}}
\sum_{{\mathtt k} \in \Lambda_{{\mathtt j}}}  \ell_1^d\, J(B_{{\mathtt k}}) \, \Big\{\,
{\mathtt p}_h({\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}})
\,-\, E_{\nu^n_{\rho(\cdot)} } \big[\,
{\mathtt p}_h({\textsf m}_{{\mathtt k}}) \,\big]
\,-\, 
\big(\, W_{{\mathtt p}_h}   ({\textsf m}_{2, {\mathtt j}})
- E_{\nu^n_{\rho(\cdot)} } [\, W_{{\mathtt p}_h}   ({\textsf m}_{2, {\mathtt j}})  \, ] \,\big)
\, \Big\}\,
f\, d\nu^n_{\rho(\cdot)}
\nonumber
\\
&  \le\, \frac{\delta'}{8} \, n^2 \,  I_n  ( f ; \nu^n_{\rho (\cdot)} )
\,+\, {\mathfrak a}_{3,3}\, \Vert J\Vert_{C^1}  \, H_n (f\,|\, \nu^n_{\rho(\cdot)}) \,+\,
e^{({\mathfrak c}_{\rm LS}/\delta')
\, [1+{\mathfrak a}_{3,3}]\,[1 + \Vert J\Vert_{C^1}]} \,n^{3/2 - 4{\mathtt e}} 
\end{align}
for all $n\ge n_1$. The right-hand side of Theorem \ref{s26} has many
terms with different powers of $n$. To bound all of them by
$n^{3/2 - 4{\mathtt e}}$ we used the assumption that we selected a constant
${\mathtt e}<1/30$.

As $\ell_1 \ell_2 = n^{2/5 - 2{\mathtt e}} \ll n^{1/2}$ we need to apply
Theorem \ref{s26} once again to increase the size of the cube to reach
lengths of order $n^{1/2}$. By \eqref{111},
$W_{{\mathtt p}_h} ({\textsf m}_{2, {\mathtt j}})$ is the sum of two terms. We
examine in detail the expression
${\mathtt p}_h({\textsf m}_{2, {\mathtt j}}) \,-\, E_{\nu^n_{\rho(\cdot)} } [\, {\mathtt p}_h({\textsf m}_{2, {\mathtt j}}) \,] $. The same arguments apply to
${\mathtt q}_h({\textsf m}_{2,{\mathtt j}}) \,-\, E_{\nu^n_{\rho(\cdot)} } [\, {\mathtt q}_h({\textsf m}_{2, {\mathtt j}}) \,] $, with a simplification due to the extra
factor $\ell_1^{-d}$.
