an expression which vanishes as $h\to 0$.  This is condition {\rm (B)}
of Lemma \ref{s89}, and completes the proof of the corollary.
<!-- end proof-68 -->
<!-- remark-35: body_md -->
\label{s91}
The interest of Corollary \ref{s90} lies in the extra term $b_n$,
which permits the modulus of continuity in time to deteriorate as
$n\to\infty$, provided it does so at a rate which vanishes in the
limit.  On the other hand, one loses the H\"older exponent: the bound
has to be linear in $h$.

The reason is that Corollary \ref{s90} appeals to Lemma \ref{s89}
directly, whereas Corollary \ref{s67} passes through the fractional
Sobolev norm of Lemma \ref{s63}.  Bounding
$\Vert {\mathtt x} \Vert_{\dot W^{\sigma, 1} (0, T ; {\mathcal H}_{- {\mathtt r}})}$ requires
the integrability of $|t-s|^{b-\sigma-1}$, which fails for a bound of
the form $\beta_m (|t-s| + b_n)$, since the term $b_n$ contributes
$b_n \int_0^T\!\!\int_0^T |t-s|^{-1-\sigma} ds\, dt = \infty$.
<!-- end remark-35 -->
<!-- lemma-45: body_md -->
\label{s92}
Fix ${\mathtt r} \in {\mathbb R}$ and a sequence $({\mathtt x}^n : n\ge 1)$ of random
elements of $L^1(0,T;{\mathcal H}_{-{\mathtt r}})$.  Suppose that there exist
${\mathtt r}' < {\mathtt r}$, $b>0$, a sequence $\{\beta_m : m \in {\mathbb Z}^d\}$
with
\begin{equation*}
{\mathfrak b} \;:=\; \sum_{m\in {\mathbb Z}^d} \beta_m \, \gamma_m^{-{\mathtt r}'/2}\,
\omega^{-1/2}_m \;<\;\infty\;,
\end{equation*}
and non-negative random variables $\Theta_n$ such that
$\lim_{A\to\infty} \limsup_{n\to\infty} {\mathbb P}[\Theta_n > A] = 0$, and,
almost surely,
\begin{equation}
\label{237}
\int_0^T \big|\, \< {\mathtt x}^n (t) ,\, \phi_m\>\, \big| \, dt \;\le\;
\Theta_n\, \beta_m \;, \qquad
\big|\, \< {\mathtt x}^n (t) - {\mathtt x}^n(s) ,\, \phi_m\>\, \big| \;\le\;
\Theta_n\, \beta_m\, |t-s|^{b}
\end{equation}
for all $m \in {\mathbb Z}^d$ and $0\le s<t\le T$.  Then the sequence of
laws of ${\mathtt x}^n$ is tight in $L^1(0,T;{\mathcal H}_{-{\mathtt r}})$.
<!-- end lemma-45 -->
<!-- proof-69: body_md -->
It is enough to check the two conditions of Lemma \ref{s89}.  By
\eqref{236} and the first bound in \eqref{237}, for all $0<t_1<t_2<T$,
\begin{equation*}
\Big\| \int_{t_1}^{t_2} {\mathtt x}^n (t)\, dt \Big\|_{{\mathcal H}_{-{\mathtt r}'}}
\;\le\;
\sum_{m} \gamma_m^{-{\mathtt r}'/2} \omega_m^{-1/2}
\int_0^T \big|\, \< {\mathtt x}^n (t) ,\, \phi_m\>\, \big| \, dt
\;\le\; {\mathfrak b} \; \Theta_n \;.
\end{equation*}
Since this bound is uniform in $t_1$, $t_2$,
${\mathbb Q}_n[\sup_{t_1<t_2}\Vert \int_{t_1}^{t_2}{\mathtt x}^n\Vert_{-{\mathtt r}'}
>A] \le {\mathbb P}[\Theta_n > A/{\mathfrak b}]$, and condition (A) of Lemma
\ref{s89} follows from the property of the sequence $\Theta_n$.

Similarly, by \eqref{236}, the second bound in \eqref{237}, as
$\gamma_m \ge 1$ and ${\mathtt r}>{\mathtt r}'$,
\begin{equation*}
\int_0^{T-h} \Vert {\mathtt x}^n(t+h) - {\mathtt x}^n(t)\Vert_{{\mathcal H}_{-{\mathtt r}}}
\, dt \;\le\; T\, {\mathfrak b}\, \Theta_n \, h^{b}
\end{equation*}
for all $0<h<T$.  Therefore, for every $\epsilon>0$, by the property
of the sequence $\Theta_n$,
\begin{equation*}
\lim_{h\to 0} \limsup_{n\to\infty} {\mathbb Q}_n\Big[ \int_0^{T-h}
\Vert {\mathtt x}^n(t+h) - {\mathtt x}^n(t)\Vert_{{\mathcal H}_{-{\mathtt r}}}\, dt >
\epsilon \Big]
\;\le\;
\lim_{h\to 0}  \limsup_{n\to\infty} {\mathbb P}\Big[ \Theta_n
> \frac{\epsilon}{T {\mathfrak b}\,
h^{b}} \Big] \,=\, 0 \;.
\end{equation*}
This proves condition (B) of Lemma \ref{s89}.
<!-- end proof-69 -->
<!-- lemma-46: body_md -->
\label{s73}
Let ${\mathbb P}_1$, ${\mathbb P}_2$ be two probability measures on
$L^1 (0,T; {\mathcal H}_{- {\mathtt r}})$. Suppose that
\begin{equation*}
E_{{\mathbb P}_1} \big[\, {\mathtt F}(X) \,\big]
\,=\,
E_{{\mathbb P}_2} \big[\, {\mathtt F}(X) \,\big]
\end{equation*}
for all ${\mathtt F}\in {\mathscr A}$. Then, ${\mathbb P}_1 = {\mathbb P}_2$.
<!-- end lemma-46 -->
<!-- proof-70: body_md -->
We have seen at the beginning of this section that
$L^1 (0,T; {\mathcal H}_{- {\mathtt r}})$ is a separable Banach space. It is thus a
complete and separable metric space. Since ${\mathscr A}$ is an algebra of
bounded and continuous functions which separates points, the result
follows from \cite[Proposition 3.4.5]{ek09}.
<!-- end proof-70 -->
<!-- lemma-47: body_md -->
\label{s72}
For any ${\mathfrak g}\in L^\infty(0,T; {\mathcal H}_{{\mathtt r}})$ and any $\epsilon>0$,
there exist $q'\ge 1$, disjoint open intervals $I_j$ in $[0,T]$, and
elements ${\mathfrak g}_j\in {\mathcal H}_{{\mathtt r}}$, $1\le j\le q'$, such that
${\mathfrak g}_\epsilon \in L^\infty(0,T; {\mathcal H}_{{\mathtt r}})$ defined by
\begin{gather*}
{\mathfrak g}_\epsilon (s) = \sum_{j=1}^{q'} {\mathfrak g}_j {\mathtt 1}_{I_j} (s) 
\;\;\text{satisfies the bounds}
\\ 
\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{0\le s\le T} \Vert {\mathfrak g}_\epsilon (s)\Vert_{{\mathcal H}_{{\mathtt r}}}
\,\le\;
\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{0\le s\le T} \Vert {\mathfrak g} (s)\Vert_{{\mathcal H}_{{\mathtt r}}} \,,\quad
\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{s\in I} \Vert {\mathfrak g}_\epsilon (s) - {\mathfrak g} (s)\Vert_{{\mathcal H}_{{\mathtt r}}} \,\le\; \epsilon\,, \;\;
\lambda ([0,T] \setminus I) \,\le\, \epsilon\,,
\end{gather*}
where $I = \cup_j I_j$, and $\lambda$ stands for the Lebesgue
measure.
<!-- end lemma-47 -->
<!-- proof-71: body_md -->
By \cite[Lemma 1.2.19]{hnvw16}, the simple functions are dense in
$ L^\infty(0,T; {\mathcal H}_{{\mathtt r}})$ with respect to the convergence in
measure: for any ${\mathfrak g}\in L^\infty(0,T; {\mathcal H}_{{\mathtt r}})$ and any
$\epsilon>0$, there exist $q\ge 1$, measurable subsets $E_j$ of
$[0,T]$, and elements ${\mathfrak g}_j\in {\mathcal H}_{{\mathtt r}}$, $1\le j\le q$, such that
${\mathfrak g}_\epsilon \in L^\infty(0,T; {\mathcal H}_{{\mathtt r}})$ defined by
\begin{gather*}
{\mathfrak g}_\epsilon (s) = \sum_{j=1}^q {\mathfrak g}_j {\mathtt 1}_{E_j} (s) 
\;\;\text{satisfies the bounds}
\\ 
\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{0\le s\le T} \Vert {\mathfrak g}_\epsilon (s)\Vert_{{\mathcal H}_{{\mathtt r}}}
\,\le\;
\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{0\le s\le T} \Vert {\mathfrak g} (s)\Vert_{{\mathcal H}_{{\mathtt r}}} \,,\quad
\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{s\in E} \Vert {\mathfrak g}_\epsilon (s) - {\mathfrak g} (s)\Vert_{{\mathcal H}_{{\mathtt r}}} \,\le\; \epsilon\,, \;\;
\lambda ([0,T] \setminus E) \,\le\, \epsilon\,,
\end{gather*}
where $E = \cup_j E_j$, and $\lambda$ stands for the Lebesgue
measure. 

Since the Lebesgue measure on $[0,T]$ is regular, we may replace in
the previous assertion simple functions by step functions, that is,
replace the measurable sets $E_j$, $1\le j\le q$, by open disjoint
intervals $I_{k}$, $1\le k\le q'$, at the price of enlarging the
exceptional set by at most $\epsilon$.
<!-- end proof-71 -->
<!-- corollary-20: body_md -->
\label{s74}
Let ${\mathbb P}_1$, ${\mathbb P}_2$ be two probability measures on
$L^1 (0,T; {\mathcal H}_{- {\mathtt r}})$. Suppose that
\begin{equation*}
E_{{\mathbb P}_1} \big[\, {\mathtt F}(X) \,\big]
\,=\,
E_{{\mathbb P}_2} \big[\, {\mathtt F}(X) \,\big]
\end{equation*}
for all all ${\mathtt F}\in {\mathscr A}_{\rm fdd}$. Then, ${\mathbb P}_1 = {\mathbb P}_2$.
<!-- end corollary-20 -->
<!-- proof-72: body_md -->
By Lemma \ref{s73}, it is enough to extend the identity to functions
${\mathtt F}$ in ${\mathscr A}$. Fix such a function. By definition, there exists
$p\ge 1$, ${\mathfrak g}_1, \dots, {\mathfrak g}_p \in L^\infty (0,T; {\mathcal H}_{{\mathtt r}})$, and
a continuous bounded function $F\colon {\mathbb R}^p \to {\mathbb R}$ for which
\eqref{182} holds. We assume that $p=1$, the same proof applies to the
general case. Hence,
\begin{equation*}
{\mathtt F}(X) \,=\, F \Big( \int_{0}^{T} \< X_s , {\mathfrak g} (s)\> \, ds\,\Big)
\end{equation*}
for some continuous function $F$ and ${\mathfrak g}\in  L^\infty (0,T; {\mathcal H}_{{\mathtt r}})$. For $n\ge 1$, denote by ${\mathfrak g}_n\in  L^\infty (0,T; {\mathcal H}_{{\mathtt r}})$ the approximation given by Lemma \ref{s72} with
$\epsilon=1/n$. Let
\begin{equation*}
{\mathtt F}_n(X) \,=\, F \Big( \int_{0}^{T} \< X_s , {\mathfrak g}_n(s) \> \, ds\,\Big)\,.
\end{equation*}
By definition of ${\mathfrak g}_n$, ${\mathtt F}_n$ belongs to ${\mathscr A}_{\rm fdd}$,
and, for each $X\in L^1 (0,T; {\mathcal H}_{- {\mathtt r}})$, 
\begin{equation*}
\lim_{n\to\infty} \int_{0}^{T} \< X_s , {\mathfrak g}_n(s) \> \, ds  \, = \,
\int_{0}^{T} \< X_s , {\mathfrak g}(s) \> \, ds\,.
\end{equation*}
Thus, as $F$ is continuous, 
$\lim_n {\mathtt F}_n (X) = {\mathtt F}(X)$. By the dominated convergence
theorem, and by hypothesis,
\begin{equation*}
E_{{\mathbb P}_1} \big[\, {\mathtt F}(X) \,\big] \,=\,
\lim_{n\to\infty} E_{{\mathbb P}_1} \big[\, {\mathtt F}_n (X) \,\big] 
\,=\,
\lim_{n\to\infty} E_{{\mathbb P}_2} \big[\, {\mathtt F}_n (X) \,\big]
\,=\, E_{{\mathbb P}_2} \big[\, {\mathtt F}(X) \,\big] 
\,,
\end{equation*}
which completes the proof of the corollary.
<!-- end proof-72 -->
<!-- theorem-9: body_md -->
\label{s83}
There exists a positive constant ${\mathfrak c}_{\rm LS}$ such that
\begin{equation*}
\int f\, \ln f\, \, d \nu^{\rm c}_{n, {\textsf M}}   \,\le\,
{\mathfrak c}_{\rm LS}\, n^2\, I_{n} (f \,;\, \nu^{\rm c}_{n, {\textsf M}} )
\end{equation*}
for all densities $f$ with respect to $\nu^{\rm c}_{n, {\textsf M}}$, $0\le
{\textsf M}\le |\Sigma_{n}|$, $n\ge 1$.
<!-- end theorem-9 -->
<!-- corollary-21: body_md -->
\label{s84}
There exists a positive constant ${\mathfrak c}_{\rm SG}$ (bounded by
$(1/2) {\mathfrak c}_{\rm LS}$) such that
\begin{equation*}
\int g^2 \, \, d \nu^{\rm c}_{n, {\textsf M}}   \,\le\,
{\mathfrak c}_{\rm SG}\, n^2\, I_{n} (g \,;\, \nu^{\rm c}_{n, {\textsf M}} )
\end{equation*}
for all functions $g$ such that
$\int g \, d\nu^{\rm c}_{n, {\textsf M}} =0$, $0\le {\textsf M}\le |\Sigma_{n}|$,
$n\ge 1$.
<!-- end corollary-21 -->
<!-- lemma-48: body_md -->
\label{l42}
For each cylinder function $f$, 
\begin{equation*}
f(\eta) \,-\, E_{\nu^n_{\rho(\cdot)} } [f]  \,=\,
(\Pi^1_{\rho(\cdot)}  f)  (\eta)
\;+\; (\Pi^2_{\rho(\cdot)} f) (\eta) \;.
\end{equation*}
<!-- end lemma-48 -->
<!-- proof-73: body_md -->
By \eqref{13}, 
\begin{equation*}
f(\eta) \,-\, E_{\nu^n_{\rho(\cdot)} } [f] \,=\,
\sum_{B \subset A} c_B \, [\, \eta_B - \rho_B]\,.
\end{equation*}
Rewrite the previous sum as
\begin{equation*}
\sum_{B \subset A} c_B \, \Big \{\, \prod_{z\in B} [\, \xi_z +
\rho(z/n) \,] - \rho_B\, \Big\} \,=\,
\sum_{B \subset A} c_B \,  \sum_{\varnothing \subsetneq C\subset B} \xi_C \,
\rho_{B\setminus C}
\,=\, \sum_{\varnothing \subsetneq C\subset A} \xi_C \,
\sum_{C\subset B \subset A} c_B \,   \rho_{B\setminus C} \,.
\end{equation*}
Separating the singletons from the rest yields that
\begin{equation*}
f(\eta) \,-\, E_{\nu^n_{\rho(\cdot)} } [f]  \,=\,
\sum_{z\in A} \xi_z \,
\sum_{\{z\} \subset B \subset A} c_B \,   \rho_{B\setminus \{z\}}
\,+\,
\sum_{C\subset A, |C|\ge 2} \xi_C \,
\sum_{C\subset B \subset A} c_B \,   \rho_{B\setminus C}
\end{equation*}
To complete the proof of the lemma, it remains to recall the
identities \eqref{16}, \eqref{15}.
<!-- end proof-73 -->
<!-- remark-36: body_md -->
\label{rm2}
The above computation shows that the term
$E_{\nu^n_{\rho(\cdot)} } [f]$ removes the constants from $f(\eta)$,
and that the expansion
\begin{equation*}
f \,-\,  E_{\nu^n_{\rho(\cdot)} } [f] \,-\,  (\Pi^1_{\rho(\cdot)} f) ( \eta)
\end{equation*}
only contains terms of degree $2$ or larger.
<!-- end remark-36 -->
<!-- lemma-49: body_md -->
\label{s34}
For all $0<\rho<1$, $1\le j\le d$, $x\neq 0$,
$E_{\nu_{\rho} } \, [\, \tau_{x} h_{j} \, [\, \eta_0 -\rho\,] \, ]
\,=\,0$, and
\begin{equation*}
E_{\nu_{\rho} } \, \big[\, h_{j}
\, [\, \eta_0 -\rho\,] \, \big] \,=\, \chi(\rho) \,
E_{\nu_{\rho} } \, \big[\, c_{0,e_j}(\eta) \, \big] \,.
\end{equation*}
<!-- end lemma-49 -->
<!-- proof-74: body_md -->
Fix $1\le j\le d$.  The proof is based on the following
observation. Let ${\mathtt j}_{y,y+{\boldsymbol e}_k}$, $y\in {\mathbb Z}^d$,
$1\le k\le d$, be the instantaneous current over the bond
$(y,y+{\boldsymbol e}_k)$:
${\color{blue} {\mathtt j}_{y,y+{\boldsymbol e}_k}} := c_{y,y+{\boldsymbol e}_k} (\eta) \, [\, \eta_y -
\eta_{y+{\boldsymbol e}_k} \,] $.  As $c_{0,e_k} (\cdot)$ does not depend on
$\eta_0$, $\eta_{e_k}$,
\begin{equation}
\label{137}
E_{\nu_{\rho} } \, \Big[\, {\mathtt j}_{x, x+ e_k} (\eta) 
\,  [\, \eta_0 -\rho\,] \, \Big] \,=\, 0 \quad \text{if $x$ and
$x+e_k\neq 0$}\,.
\end{equation}

By \eqref{11b}, 
\begin{equation*}
\begin{aligned}
& \tau_{z(x,p)}  h_{j} \, =\,  \tau_{z(x,0)}  h_j
\,-\, \sum_{r=0}^{p- 1} {\mathtt j} _{z(x,r),
z(x,r+1) }\,,\quad \text{for}\;\; p\ge 1
\\
& \tau_{z(x,p)}  h_{j} \, =\, \tau_{z(x,0)}  h_j
\,+\, \sum_{r=p}^{- 1} {\mathtt j} _{z(x,r),
z(x,r+1) }\,,\quad \text{for}\;\; p\le -\, 1\,,
\end{aligned}
\end{equation*}
where
${\color{blue} z(x,r)} : = \sum_{i\neq j} x_i\, {\boldsymbol e}_i\, +\, r\, {\boldsymbol e}_j$.
Therefore, if $p\ge 1$, 
\begin{equation}
\label{139}
E_{\nu_{\rho} } \, \Big[\, \tau_{z(x,p)}   h_{j}
\, [\, \eta_0 -\rho\,] \, \Big] \,=\,
E_{\nu_{\rho} } \, \Big[\, \tau_{z(x,0)}  h_{j}
\, [\, \eta_0 -\rho\,] \, \Big] \,-\,
\sum_{r=0}^{p- 1}
E_{\nu_{\rho} } \, \Big[\, 
\, [\, \eta_0 -\rho\,] \, {\mathtt j} _{z(x,r), z(x,r+1)}
\,\Big]\,.
\end{equation}
A similar formula holds for  $p\le -1$.

Fix $k\neq j$. In this case, if $x_k\neq 0$, then $z(x,r) \neq 0$ for
all $r\in {\mathbb Z}$. Hence, by \eqref{137}, the second term on the
right-hand side of the previous identity vanishes. Thus, for all
$x\in {\mathbb Z}^d$ such that $x_k\neq 0$,
\begin{equation*}
E_{\nu_{\rho} } \, [\, \tau_{z(x,p)}   h_{j} \, [\, \eta_0 -\rho\,] \, ]
\,=\,
E_{\nu_{\rho} } \, [\, \tau_{z(x,0)}    h_{j} \, [\, \eta_0 -\rho\,] \, ] \,.
\end{equation*}
Consider $p$ sufficiently large for the support of $\tau_{z(x,p)}  h_{j}$
not to contain $0$. In this case, the left-hand side of the previous
identity vanishes. This implies that the right-hand side vanishes,
which in turn yields that the left-hand side vanishes for all $p$.
Therefore,
\begin{equation}
\label{138}
E_{\nu_{\rho} } \, [\, \tau_x h_{j} \, [\, \eta_0 -\rho\,] \, ]
\,=\, 0\quad\text{if}\;\; x_k \neq 0 \quad \text{for some}\;\;
k\neq j \,.
\end{equation}


It remains to consider the case $x= p {\boldsymbol e}_j$ for some $p\in{\mathbb Z}$.
By \eqref{139} and \eqref{137},
\begin{equation*}
E_{\nu_{\rho} } \, \Big[\, \tau_{p{\boldsymbol e}_j}  h_{j}
\, [\, \eta_0 -\rho\,] \, \Big] \,=\,
E_{\nu_{\rho} } \, \Big[\, h_{j}
\, [\, \eta_0 -\rho\,] \, \Big] \, - \, \chi(\rho) \,
E_{\nu_{\rho} } \, \Big[\, c_{0,e_j}(\eta) \, \Big] 
\end{equation*}
for $p\neq 0$. For $p$ large the left-hand side vanishes. This proves
that the right-hand side vanishes, and, therefore, that the left-hand
side vanishes for all $p\neq 0$.
<!-- end proof-74 -->
<!-- corollary-22: body_md -->
\label{s21}
For every $1\le j, k\le d$, $0<\rho<1$, 
\begin{equation*}
E_{\nu_{\rho} } \, \Big[\, h_{j} \sum_{x\in {\mathbb Z}^d} x_k\, 
\,  [\, \eta_x -\rho\,] \, \Big] \,=\, 0\,.
\end{equation*}
As $h_j$ is a cylinder function, we may replace the sum over ${\mathbb Z}^d$
by a sum over a finite set $A$ which contains the support of $h_j$.
<!-- end corollary-22 -->
<!-- proof-75: body_md -->
Fix $1\le j\le d$.  
As $\nu_\rho$ is translation invariant, the expression appearing in
the statement of the corollary is equal to
\begin{equation*}
-\, \sum_{x\in A} x_k\, E_{\nu_{\rho} } \, \Big[\, \tau_x h_{j}
\, [\, \eta_0 -\rho\,] \, \Big] \,.
\end{equation*}
The assertion thus follows from the previous lemma.
<!-- end proof-75 -->
<!-- corollary-23: body_md -->
\label{s24}
Let $\rho\colon {\mathbb T}^d \to (0,1)$ be a density profile in
$C^2({\mathbb T}^d)$ and such that ${\mathfrak r} \le \rho(x) \le 1-{\mathfrak r}$ for some
$0<{\mathfrak r} < 1/2$. Then, there exists a finite constant $C_0$, depending
only on ${\mathfrak r}$, $\Vert \nabla \rho \Vert_\infty$, $\Vert \nabla^2 \rho
\Vert_\infty$, such that
\begin{equation}
\label{136}
\Big|\, E_{\nu^n_{\rho( \cdot)}} \, [\, h_{j} \,]
\, -\, E_{\nu_{\rho(0)}} \, [\, h_{j} \,]\, \Big|\, \le \, C_0 \,
\frac{1}{n^2} \,\cdot
\end{equation}
<!-- end corollary-23 -->
<!-- proof-76: body_md -->
We may rewrite the first expectation as
\begin{equation*}
E_{\nu^n_{\rho( \cdot)}} \, [\, h_{j} \,] \,=\, 
E_{\nu_{\rho} } \, \Big[\, h_{j}  \,
\exp\Big\{ {\sum_{x\in A} \eta_x \, \ln \frac{\rho(x/n)}{\rho} \,+\,
[1-\eta_x]\, } \ln \frac{1-\rho(x/n)}{1-\rho} \,\Big\}\, \Big]\,,
\end{equation*}
where $A$ is a cube centered at the origin, sufficiently large to
contain the support of $h_j$ and $\rho = \rho(0)$.  As the exponential
has mean $1$ with respect to $\nu_{\rho} $, we may write the
difference \eqref{136} as
\begin{equation*}
E_{\nu_{\rho} } \, \Big[\, \{ \, h_{j}
-  E_{\nu_{\rho} }  [h_{j} ]  \} \,
\exp\Big\{ {\sum_{x\in A} \eta_x \, \ln \frac{\rho(x/n)}{\rho} \,+\,
[1-\eta_x]\, } \ln \frac{1-\rho(x/n)}{1-\rho} \,\Big\}\, \Big]\,.
\end{equation*}
Since $\rho(\cdot)$ is Lipschitz-continuous, the expression inside
braces is of order $1/n$. This expectation is thus equal to
\begin{equation*}
E_{\nu_{\rho} } \, \Big[\, \{ \, h_{j}
-  E_{\nu_{\rho} }  [h_{j} ]  \} \,
\sum_{x\in A} [\eta_x -\rho] \, \ln \frac{\rho(x/n)}{\rho} \,-\,
[\eta_x - \rho]\,  \ln \frac{1-\rho(x/n)}{1-\rho} \, \Big]
\,+\, {\mathfrak R}_n \,,
\end{equation*}
where ${\mathfrak R}_n$ is a remainder, whose value may change from line to
line and such that $|{\mathfrak R}_n|\le C_0 n^{-2}$ for some finite constant
$C_0$ depending only on ${\mathfrak r}$, $\Vert \nabla \rho \Vert_\infty$,
$\Vert \nabla^2 \rho \Vert_\infty$. We subtracted the expectation of
$\eta_x$ because $h_j - E_{\nu_{\rho} } [h_{j} ]$ has zero-mean. We
may now remove the expectation of $h_j$ and expand $\rho(\cdot)$ to
write the previous equation as
\begin{equation*}
\frac{1}{n}\, \sum_{k=1}^d (\partial_{x_k} \rho)(0)
\sum_{x\in A} E_{\nu_{\rho} } \, \Big[\, h_{j}
\, x_k\, \frac{\eta_x -\rho}{\chi(\rho)} \, \, \Big]
\,+\, {\mathfrak R}_n \,.
\end{equation*}
By Corollary \ref{s21}, the first term vanishes, which completes the
proof of the corollary.
<!-- end proof-76 -->
<!-- lemma-50: body_md -->
\label{s56}
Assume that $d\le 3$ and that
$H_n (\mu_n \,|\, \nu^n_{u_0(\cdot)}) = o(n^{d/2})$.
Fix $0\le t\le T$, $G$ in $C^\infty({\mathbb T}^d)$. Then,
$X^n_t(G) - X^n_0(P_{0,t}G) -M^{n,t}_t(G)$ converges to $0$ in
$L^1({\mathbb P}_{\mu_n})$.
<!-- end lemma-50 -->
<!-- proof-77: body_md -->
Recall formula \eqref{145} for $(\partial_r + L_n) \, X^n_r(F)$. Here
as the test function is time dependent, we have an extra term. More
precisely, as $\partial_r P_{r,t} G\,=\, -\, {\mathcal A}_r P_{r,t} G$,
\begin{equation*}
(\partial_r + L_n) X^n_r(P_{r,t}G ) \;=\;
R^n_r(P_{r,t} G) \;+\; B^n_r(P_{r,t} G) \, +\, {\textsf D}^{(n)}_r (P_{r,t} G)\;, 
\end{equation*}
where ${\textsf D}^{(n)}_r (\cdot)$ is the deterministic remainder
introduced in \eqref{145} and satisfying the bound
\begin{equation}
\label{189}
|\, {\textsf D}^{(n)}_r (P_{r,t} G) \,| \,\le\,
{\mathfrak a}_{3,4} (\{h_j : 1\le j\le d\}) \, \Vert
P_{r,t} G\Vert_{C^2} \, n^{(d/2)-2}\,.
\end{equation}
In the penultimate displayed equation, for a function
$H$ in $C^4({\mathbb T}^d)$, $R_r^n(H)$, $B_r^n(H)$ are given by
\begin{equation}
\label{147}
\begin{gathered}
{\color{blue} R^n_r(H)} \; :=\; \frac{1}{n^{d/2}} \sum_{j=1}^d
\sum_{x\in{\mathbb T}_n^d}
\big\{ \, (\Delta^n_j H)  -
(\partial^2_{x_j}  H ) \,\big\}(x/n)\,
D_j (u(r,x/n))  \,[\, \eta_x^n(r) - u(r,x/n) \,]  \;,
\\
{\color{blue} B^n_r(H)} \; :=\; \frac{1}{n^{d/2}} \sum_{j=1}^d
\sum_{x\in{\mathbb T}_n^d}
(\Delta^n_j H)  (x/n)\, 
\Pi_{u(r, \cdot), h_j}  (x, \eta^n(r))  \,.
\end{gathered}
\end{equation}
By a fourth order Taylor expansion,
$| (\Delta^n_j H) - (\partial^2_{x_j} H )| \le C_0 \, \Vert
H\Vert_{C^4}\, n^{-2}$ for some finite constant $C_0$. Thus,
$R^n_r(P_{r,t} G)$ fulfills the same bound \eqref{189} with the $C^2$
norm replaced by the $C^4$ norm.  Therefore,
\begin{equation}
\label{146}
X^n_t(G) \;=\;  X^n_0(P_{0,t}G)
\;+\; M^{n,t}_t(G) \;+\; \int_0^t
B^n_r(P_{r,t} G)  \; dr \, +\, \int_0^t {\mathfrak R}^n_r (P_{r,t} G) \, dr \;,
\end{equation}
where the remainder
${\color{blue} {\mathfrak R}^n_r (H)} := {\textsf D}^{(n)}_r (H) + R^n_r(H) $ satisfies
\eqref{189} with the $C^2$ norm replaced by the $C^4$ norm.  To
complete the proof, it remains to recall that, by Theorem \ref{t02},
$\int_0^t B^n_r(P_{r,t} G) \; dr$ converges to $0$ in
$L^1({\mathbb P}_{\mu_n})$.
<!-- end proof-77 -->
